It writes personal exposure scripts for each user. Five therapists joined a formative review, and 19 people with symptoms took part in a user study. Scenarios stayed within a helpful tolerance window, the authors report. Users still wanted better continuity and customization.
arxiv-2603-26033: Xing and co-authors improve few-shot action recognition by using multimodal models as a knowledge source. Past work made captions from video, then turned them back into features. Their FSAR-LLaVA method uses the model's own decoder to enrich features directly. A feature module splits and boosts visual and text signals. Flexible prompts shape outputs that guide prototype building for each class. A training-free matching metric then picks the most decisive cues. The authors report top results across tasks with few trainable parameters.
arxiv-2603-26733: Phetmanee builds a formal theory of throughput for AI pipelines in cybersecurity work. A pipeline is a chain of stages, and its throughput equals the slowest stage's capacity. He proves five theorems about what happens when stage capacities gain multipliers of at least one. Throughput stays flat exactly when some bottleneck keeps a multiplier of one. When human-run stages are pinned at one, they cap the whole chain, and the cap is tight. Paired attacker and defender chains follow a matching rule based on relative gains.
arxiv-2603-26833: Jiang and Milani Fard present SPARK, an open-source toolchain for secure predictive autoscaling in Kubernetes. Standard autoscalers react slowly to traffic spikes. They also cannot tell a real flash crowd from a DDoS attack. SPARK uses an eBPF network layer to enforce security rules in the kernel. Predictive models then guide scaling decisions ahead of demand. In tests, timeout errors fell by 32 percent during sudden surges. New pods also gained fast network setup and layer 7 isolation.
arxiv-2603-26933: Ziegler and co-authors study how weak measurements monitor the return behavior of quantum walks. For strong monitoring, the mean return time is quantized by a winding number. Here an ancilla coupling watches the walk without fully collapsing it. The mean return time then obeys a scaling relation in the measurement strength. A matching relation was known for random-time monitoring, hinting at shared effects. The authors link the weak monitoring to the walk's unitary evolution. Convergent perturbation theory controls that connection.
arxiv-2603-27033: Lawrence and co-authors present RealBirdID, a benchmark for bird identification that rewards honest abstention. In the wild, a single photo often cannot settle a fine-grained species call. Cues may be hidden, or the answer may need the bird's song. RealBirdID pairs answerable images with curated unanswerable ones carrying labeled reasons. Models must name the species or abstain with a concrete rationale. Top multimodal models scored under 13 percent on the answerable set. Stronger classifiers were not better calibrated to abstain, either.
arxiv-2603-27333: Li and co-authors present ComBench, a repo-level benchmark for repairing compilation errors in real projects. Existing benchmarks use isolated single files and miss repo complexity. ComBench mines real build failures from GitHub CI histories of large open-source projects. Its pipeline extracts ground-truth repair patches from version history. A reproduction step rebuilds the short-lived build setups. Every sample is run-verified before joining the benchmark. GPT-5 fixed syntax in 73 percent of cases but only 41 percent in meaning.
arxiv-2603-27633: Mei and co-authors study how parents steer AI help in talks with children. Such chats are sensitive and open-ended. Fixed support modes adapt poorly as topics shift. A co-design phase with eight parents shaped a probe tool. COMPASS lets parents mix support functions live. Lab trials then ran with twenty-one parent-child pairs. Support modes shifted with context in clear patterns. Three parent strategy types emerged from the data.
arxiv-2603-27933: Wang and co-authors design car interfaces that honor shared urban space. Driverless cars can erode the feel of pedestrian zones. Three place-based external displays are proposed. One upgrades a standard intent display. Others weave content and form into the place itself. Twenty-five people tried them in virtual reality. Think-aloud, interviews, and surveys capture reactions. Place-based designs boost reassurance and aesthetics. Perceived safety tracks user experience closely.
arxiv-2603-28033: Karakaş builds new tools for dependency parsing in Pomak, an endangered Slavic language with wide dialect variation and no standard form. A parser trained on the Greek variety's treebank is first tested on the Turkish variety from Uzunköprü. The dialect gap hurts accuracy. Karakaş then annotates 650 Turkish-variety sentences by hand, and fine-tuning on them lifts accuracy a lot. Mixing both dialects in training helps further.
arxiv-2603-28233: Do and four co-authors present TwinMixing, a light model that segments drivable area and lanes for self-driving cars. The network shares one encoder and gives each task its own decoder. A pyramid mixing module widens the view cheaply with grouped and dilated convolutions plus channel shuffles. Each decoder blends a sharp learned branch with a smooth free one. On BDD100K, the base model hit 92.0% mIoU for drivable area with just 0.43 million parameters.
arxiv-2603-28333: Yun and Yang fill in the hidden parts of objects in photos by borrowing world knowledge from multimodal language models. Amodal completion matters for self-driving cars and robots, yet image-only generators lack common sense about shapes. Their AmodalCG calls the language model only when an object is heavily covered. The model then judges how much is missing and what it should look like. A generator uses that guidance and polishes the result in rounds.
arxiv-2603-28533: Xu and six co-authors train agents to answer questions by walking a knowledge graph, in their GraphWalker framework. Good walking agents are scarce because training paths are few and fixed routes limit exploration. GraphWalker first teaches on synthetic trails from constrained random walks, giving a broad sense of the graph. A short second stage on expert trails adds reflection and error recovery. The recipe topped CWQ and WebQSP scores and held up on unseen reasoning paths.
arxiv-2603-29233: Kim and Fan study the ski rental problem with distributional advice. The problem models the choice between renting repeatedly and buying once. Classical methods guard the worst case. Learning-based methods use point predictions. Their framework uses full predicted distributions of unknown quality. For perfect predictions, they compute the optimal day to buy. A clamp policy keeps thresholds safe when predictions err. A water-filling method handles the randomized case. Experiments show better consistency than point-prediction baselines.
arxiv-2603-29433: Maya-Barbecho and García-Ramos study the shapes of odd-mass niobium isotopes. These nuclei sit where shapes can coexist and shift in phase. They use a boson-fermion model that mixes two kinds of states. Regular and intruder states both interact with the unpaired nucleon. They map energy surfaces for isotopes from mass 93 to 103. The maps show both shape coexistence and crossing along the chain. A crossing near neutron number 60 marks a phase transition. The lone nucleon makes that shift less abrupt.
arxiv-2603-29733: Leonardi and co-authors test whether synthetic data can improve hand-object contact detection in first-person images. They run broad trials on the VISOR, EgoHOS, and ENIGMA-51 datasets. With fake data plus just 10% real labels, scores beat models trained on real data alone. Gains reach 11.69 points on ENIGMA-51. Closer matches in objects, grasps, and scenes help more. The team releases a generation pipeline and the HOI-Synth benchmark.
arxiv-2603-30033: Klein and co-authors generalize how attention layers get approximated. Methods like grouped-query and latent attention use odd low-rank factorizations. What they truly approximate stays murky under classic theory. Their Tucker Attention views attention weights through one tensor factorization frame. It needs about ten times fewer parameters at matched validation scores. Grouped-query, latent, and standard attention all appear as special cases. The frame also exposes the real ranks those methods reach. MLA gets useful simplifications from the view.
arxiv-2604-00033: Maiti deforms usual spectral geometry by feeding dissipation into the Dirac operator of a spectral triple. The source is a set of Lindblad jump operators. The new operator stays of Laplace type, so its heat-trace expansion keeps the standard form with shifted coefficients. For a simple scalar deformation, the first-order correction vanishes outright, pushing the first real dissipative effect to fourth order. Maiti then uses that heat trace to define a size-linked effective spectral dimension.
arxiv-2604-00133: Codi and five colleagues study what vaccines do after infection, for the naturally infected, people who would catch the disease even without a shot. Usual methods look only at the doomed stratum, those infected with or without vaccination, which understates benefit by leaving out cases the shot prevents. The authors set bounds under weak rules and pin down single values under an exclusion rule or partial principal ignorability. A rotavirus trial reanalysis then shows a shielding effect on antibiotic use on those grounds, where cruder group analyses show little.
arxiv-2604-00733: Kohlberger introduces Spectral Compact Training, replacing dense weights with truncated SVD factors, so no full dense matrix ever materialises. Gradients flow through the factors via backpropagation, with U and V returned to the Stiefel manifold by QR decomposition after each step. It cuts MLP-layer memory up to 199 times at rank 32, enabling training steps of 70-billion models on Steam Deck, at 7.2 GB versus 1,245 GB dense FP32 with Adam. Rank sweeps on a SmolLM2 model on an A100 test the method further.
arxiv-2604-00833: Chudnovsky and Seymour define a semi-strong minor of digraphs and a width measure for plane digraphs based on branch-composition. They show that, for any fixed plane digraph, the plane digraphs avoiding it as a semi-strong minor have bounded width. Plane digraphs in general have unbounded width. The result rests on obtaining a subdivision of the minor from a subdigraph by contracting strongly connected subdigraphs to single vertices.
arxiv-2604-01033: Boström, Carlsson, and Idini build a microscopic setup giving an optical potential from a working Hamiltonian, working out neutron scattering cross sections for bent magnesium-24, chromium-48, and chromium-50. Their approach rests on a symmetry generator grid method, treating nuclear structure and reaction readings as one. Through it, non-local optical fields could be built for any nucleus in the nuclide chart. They run reactions with four-pole bent triaxial shapes, getting results for chromium forms near mass 50 and studying the non-local optical fields.
arxiv-2604-01133: Li and Rodina recast early-universe wavefunctions as amplitude-like objects. They map tube variables onto scattering invariants. At tree level these objects match a known construction built from Cayley functions. The paper uncovers new graph-based hidden zeros that extend earlier cosmological zeros. It then uses a splitting rule dual to unitarity: a zero splits the generating graph. That split pins down tree-level wavefunctions from locality and zeros alone, without assuming unitarity.
arxiv-2604-01433: Blandino and colleagues propose multi-mode data sets linking radio signals to their physical settings. They address a lack of high-quality data for RF-based AI. RF heatmaps are complex but lack spatial and meaning context for interpretation. Settings span indoor and outdoor scenes with human activities from walking to subtle gestures. Co-registration and digital replicas for voxel-level annotation enable AI research. Key tasks are predicting RF heatmaps from visual data and inferring scene semantics from RF signals, a new form of RF-based perception.
arxiv-2604-01733: Akarsu and colleagues benchmark ten retrieval methods for question answering over documents mixing text and tables, a setting with no prior study. Their financial test set holds 23,088 queries over 7,318 documents, scored on retrieval and answer quality with paired bootstrap tests. A two-stage pipeline pairing hybrid retrieval with neural reranking reaches Recall at 5 of 0.816, beating every single-stage method widely. Classic BM25 beats dense retrieval on financial documents, while query expansion helps precise numerical queries little and context-aware retrieval gains.
arxiv-2604-01833: Luo and Shen challenge the idea that language pre-trained models suit visual tasks poorly because their parameters differ from vision models'. Outlier ratios differ between language and vision pre-training, making cross-modality transfer harder than cross-domain adaptation. Contrary to that idea, adding bridge training can align large language model parameters with vision tasks. Their random label bridge training needs no labels and adapts language model parameters to vision tasks. Partial bridge training helps, as certain language model layers retain properties beneficial without fine-tuning for visual tasks.
arxiv-2604-02133: Bu and Yang build a field theory for s-wave superconducting transitions with the Schwinger Keldysh method. A gauge field and a complex scalar order parameter serve as variables, and symmetry rules organize loss and fluctuation terms. Cut down, the theory gives Ginzburg Landau equations. Below the critical temperature, gauge symmetry breaks as the order parameter condenses. The Higgs mode turns slow and diffusive near the critical point, while phase fluctuations join the gauge field. Holographic checks confirm the structure and pin down its coefficients.
arxiv-2604-02233: Caroppo and colleagues trade quantum memory for time in dynamic programming. The earlier quantum algorithms speed up NP hard problems but demand large quantum random access memory, hard to build. By mixing classical methods with quantum techniques, the authors derive new time space tradeoffs that keep a speedup over classical methods while cutting memory needs. The traveling salesperson problem, for instance, gains a quantum solution with far less QRAM than before.
arxiv-2604-02533: Feng shows that a broad class of one-dimensional contact systems, usually treated as irreducibly nonlinear, hides an exact linear structure. Under an energy-based change of coordinates and time rescaling, any conservative contact system meeting monotone energy conditions becomes a harmonic oscillator, a simple spring-like system. From this he derives a universal damping law and a closed-form lower bound for the safe simulation timestep.
arxiv-2604-02733: Dhanda introduces DeltaLogic, a method for testing belief revision in logical reasoning models under minimal premise changes. Each episode asks for a conclusion, applies a tiny edit to the premises, and asks whether the conclusion should stand or change. Built from FOLIO and ProofWriter and tested on small causal models, it shows stronger initial reasoning does not imply stronger revision: Qwen3-1.7B scores 0.667 at first but only 0.467 on revision.
arxiv-2604-03033: Giacometti and four colleagues derive quantum gravity effects to gauge and Yukawa coupling beta functions via the Schwinger proper-time flow equation. In the Einstein-Hilbert truncation, they probe gauge-fixing and regulator effects of the renormalization group rules. They gauge sensitivity to unphysical values by evaluating the gravitational correction to running couplings at gravity's interactive fixed point, comparing with existing results in other schemes. They test the contributions against sizes needed for observable low-scale forecasts in the Standard Model and new physics.
arxiv-2604-03333: Jiang and colleagues steer symbolic music generation toward a chosen composer style without retraining, using a Composer Vector in latent space. A continuous steering coefficient gives smooth, interpretable control, and styles can blend seamlessly within one framework. Tests across several music models show the method guides output toward target styles, opening more flexible and interactive creative workflows.
arxiv-2604-03533: Semitsu, Kiribuchi, and Zenitani present an auto crosswalk framework that compares AI safety policy document pairs under a shared map of tasks. Using task groups from the Activity Map on AI Safety, the system pulls and maps tasks. It then gives each aspect a short summary per document, a brief comparison, and a likeness score. Model choice affects crosswalk outcomes a lot, and some document pairs yield high splits across models, while three experts agree closely.
arxiv-2604-03633: Bing Yu and colleagues studied how Hawking radiation, the glow predicted at a black hole edge, affects a quantum feature called imaginarity. In the region an outside observer can reach, rising temperature weakened the nonlocal advantage of imaginarity until it could disappear, while the hidden region showed none of it at all. Aided distillation of imaginarity also shifted with temperature, falling in the reachable region and rising in the hidden one.
arxiv-2604-03833: Hessen Bougueffa Eutamene and colleagues built SPARK-IL, a deepfake image detector that leans on frequency-domain signs. Those signs hold steadier across generators than pixel flaws, which shift from one generator to the next. That steadiness matters because new generators keep appearing. Two paths handle meaning and raw pixels, splitting each into four frequency bands handled by expert nets, then fused. When judging a new image, the fused code pulls near matches from a growing store for a majority vote. On 19 generative models it averaged 94.6 percent accuracy.
arxiv-2604-04033: Nalin Dhiman revisited claims that biological graph topology improves learning in connectome-constrained neural networks. Under weak controls, a Drosophila connectome model looked better than sparse random controls on early loss, activity, and runtime. Training both graphs from a shared random start erased the loss edge, and a degree-preserving rewired null erased the activity edge. The study concludes that earlier topology advantages largely reflect initialization and null-model confounds, not genuine biological benefit.
arxiv-2604-04333: Kahn, Horowitz and Samotin compare automation bias, over-trusting algorithmic advice, and algorithm aversion, distrusting it too soon, in West Point cadets versus the public. In a survey experiment, 236 cadets and a similar public sample did a target task. They then got advice from an algorithm or a human analyst and could revise their call. Cadets showed less cognitive distortion than the public, with better calibrated trust in algorithmic support. The authors read this as evidence that military education and AI exposure shape trust in wartime decisions.
arxiv-2604-04433: Lee and colleagues study chimera baryons, bound states of two fundamental hyperquarks and one antisymmetric hyperquark in a non-Abelian gauge group. In QCD these match normal baryons, but with top partial compositeness, spin-1/2 chimera baryons partner the top quark, driving its mass. The team runs non-perturbative lattice calculations of the chimera baryon spectrum in a Sp(4) gauge theory. In the quenched approximation they report results in the continuum and massless limits. For dynamical fermions they measure spectrum and matrix elements with a spectral density analysis.
arxiv-2604-04533: Singh and colleagues probe the boost-invariant growth of a first-order spin fluid frame that treats spin chemical potential as top-level. With a symmetric energy-momentum tensor and a saved spin tensor, they work out linked laws for heat and spin chemical potential parts. For boost-invariant set-ups, magnet-like spin chemical potential parts live on, shifting sharply with spin transport factors. With the resulting heat profiles, they work out thermal dilepton rates from quark-antiquark death, finding spin motion lifts yield over plain dissipative fluid flow.
arxiv-2604-04733: Jain and five colleagues propose a reinforcement learning framework to discover failure modes in vision-language models. Vision-language models perform strongly on benchmarks yet often misinterpret ideas such as counting, spatial logic and viewpoints. Earlier studies identified these weaknesses by hand, but efforts are costly and biased, often missing subtle details. The framework trains a questioner agent that generates queries from the target model's replies to elicit incorrect answers. The approach raises question levels by focusing on fine-grained visual details, identifying novel failure modes where models struggle.
arxiv-2604-04833: Pandey gives a cryptanalysis of the single degree Legendre pseudorandom function over extension fields. Over prime fields its security is charted, but extension-field use is new. Under passive sequential queries, a no carry fracture blocks sliding window collision attacks. Yet the fracture repeats on a cycle, and a differential signature grouping lets a foe recover the key. Under active chosen queries, a geometric sequence built from a primitive polynomial restores multiplicative structure and extends table collision attacks. Pandey proves higher degree key variants are needed for exponential security.
arxiv-2604-05233: Fujino, Fujisawa, and Ono study acceptable bundles on a partly punctured polydisk in detail. Acceptable bundles play a key role in Simpson-Mochizuki theory, so the setting matters for that theory. The article is mainly expository, walking through known material. It also gives new arguments that differ from those of Mochizuki, adding a fresh line of proof to the subject.
arxiv-2604-05333: Liu and six colleagues address a growth trap for AI agents whose skill libraries run to thousands. Loading everything swamps the context window, while simple topic search drops skills a task needs as prerequisites. Their Graph-of-Skills layer builds a graph of skill dependencies in advance, then retrieves a bounded bundle by walking dependencies backwards within a context budget. Across two benchmarks and three families it topped full loading in every block, lifting reward by seven points on one test while cutting token use by about 57 percent.
arxiv-2604-05433: Tsai, Lin, and Wang segment new object categories from a handful of examples by repurposing the frozen Segment Anything Model 3, sidestepping costly episodic training. They place support and query images side by side on one canvas so the model's promptable concept segmentation works without fine-tuning. The minimal design leads benchmarks on PASCAL-5i and COCO-20i, and the authors warn that negative prompts can weaken targets and collapse predictions.
arxiv-2604-05533: Li and nine colleagues give multimodal game agents a transferable memory called Echo, tested in Minecraft. Echo splits reusable knowledge into structure, attribute, process, function, and interaction, then retrieves and adapts past experience by analogy. From scratch, agents unlock objects 1.3 to 1.7 times faster and show burst-like chain unlocking once transferable experience lands.
arxiv-2604-05833: Costanzi and five colleagues model optical selection bias in galaxy cluster lensing from line-of-sight projections. A scale-dependent bias parametrization plus off-axis halo contributions captures two-halo profile dependence on richness boosts and redshift. Validated on a DES Y3-like catalog, the model recovers projected profile bias against mass-matched random samples.
arxiv-2604-06033: Huang and Lahoud layer an extra waveform onto standard LoRa with minimal harm to decoding. Their 2026 paper first shows any added signal disturbs the usual dechirp-and-transform demodulator. It then finds the least degrading waveforms for a power budget. A high spreading-factor signal over a low one disturbs decoding only slightly. For example, SF12 over SF7. Each low-factor interval can then carry an extra BPSK stream. Error-rate formulas match Monte Carlo simulations, and the scheme lifts spectral efficiency with a simple transceiver.
arxiv-2604-06233: Pattison, Manuali, and Lazar document blind refusal: models refusing help to evade rules without asking whether the rule deserves compliance. When rules come from illegitimate authorities, are unjust or absurd, or admit justified exceptions, refusal is a moral failure. Their dataset crosses five defeat families with 19 authority types, validated by gates and human review, and they test 18 configurations with a judge. Models refuse 75.4 percent of defeated-rule requests, even with no safety or dual-use concerns. They engage with the defeat condition yet decline, despite grasping the reasoning.
arxiv-2604-06333: Franz and four colleagues ask whether drifting models, which follow a drift field, amount to tuning a scalar loss. In general, they do not: drift fields cannot be written as gradients of scalar fields. Place-dependent scaling causes this gap, except for the Gaussian kernel. They introduce a sharp kernel and sharp-normalized drift field, conservative for radial kernels. The final field is a scalar field's gradient, tunable with stochastic gradient descent. Sharp scaling preserves first drifting performance.
arxiv-2604-06533: Farzan and Mathur offer a middle path for predicting what a concurrent program might do. Full reads-from reasoning makes prediction intractable even for simple races, while narrower commutativity reasoning stays fast but weak. Their sliced reorderings split an execution into k plus one ordered parts whose join keeps program order and reads-from rules. These slices form a rising ladder that reaches full reads-from power as k grows, and for any fixed k a constant-space streaming checker handles any regular specification.
arxiv-2604-06633: Liang and nine colleagues rebuild security testing around language models instead of bolting them onto old tools. Standalone model approaches suffer false alarms, invented flaws, shallow reasoning, and heavy token use. Their Argus system centers a team of agents that checks supply chains, works together, and draws on retrieval and ReAct reasoning to curb invention and deepen analysis. Tests show it finds more true flaws with fewer false alarms and lower cost, and it has already turned up critical zero-day flaws that earned CVE numbers.
arxiv-2604-06733: Kim and Choi explain oxygen-vacancy migration barriers in rutile oxides through bond strength. Combining density-functional theory with the bond-valence model, they split bonding into covalent and ionic parts, tracked by crystal orbital Hamilton population sums and Madelung energy. Both parts track the computed barrier closely, and their average gives a sound estimate across the oxide series. Fitting two bond-valence parameters to a large dioxide dataset then lets the barrier be estimated fast for new members of the series.
arxiv-2604-06933: Bhattacharya, Mondal, and Dewangan probe the accretion geometry of the pulsar SAX J1808 as it nears the propeller regime. From three NuSTAR and two NICER observations of its 2022 and 2025 outbursts, they fit the glow with a thermal Comptonization model and find disk reflection features. The disk edge moves outward, the glow fades, feeding slows, and ionization drops from 2022 to 2025. In 2025 the disk is cut off past the co-rotation radius, yet a Type-I burst shows matter reaching the surface, with helium burning at shallow depth.
arxiv-2604-07533: Jurado-Lasso and Jurado introduce RL-ASL, a reinforcement-learning listening framework for TSCH networks in industrial IoT settings. Standard TSCH schedulers use static slot allocations, causing idle listening and wasted power under dynamic traffic. RL-ASL chooses whether to activate or skip a scheduled slot based on real-time network conditions, pairing learning-based slot skipping with standard scheduling. Tests on FIT IoT-LAB and Cooja show up to 46 percent lower power use than baseline protocols, near-perfect reliability, and up to 96 percent lower average latency than PRIL-M.
arxiv-2604-08033: Zhou and five colleagues present IoT-Brain, a system grounding language models in sensor scheduling. Sensor networks shift from fixed monitoring to intent-driven operation, exposing a gap between semantic goals and physical sensing. Direct language-model planning proves unreliable, with gaps in representation, reasoning, and optimization. The team formalizes the choice of what to sense and when as Semantic-Spatial Sensor Scheduling. A Spatial Trajectory Graph turns open-ended planning into a graph optimization problem under a verify-before-commit rule, and IoT-Brain implements it.
arxiv-2604-08433: Franz, Kirschbaum, and Pálffy model how a Bessel beam pulse, tuned to the 8.4 electronvolt nuclear clock transition in thorium 229 doped crystals, scatters forward through the material. Because the beam's profile varies across its width and it carries orbital angular momentum, it may open excitation paths that flat plane waves cannot. Their results show beam propagation can reveal how quantization axes are distributed inside the crystal.
arxiv-2604-08633: Ribeiro, Mamede, and Ferreira tackle systematic black box testing of APIs, where interface specs say little about behavior. Their IcePick framework models API state evolution in TLA+, explores reachable states exhaustively with the TLC checker, and extracts test sequences with provable coverage via a guided traversal. A new contract language, Glacier, adds executable semantic contracts so tests verify behavior, not just status codes, and faults in multi step interactions surface.
arxiv-2604-08833: Doyle derives a shared quotient of banking APIs from four axioms: a fixed ledger, linear consent, payments that cannot reverse, and bounded credit. The axioms certify 14 aspects seen in practice and stable across regions. Morphisms allow epi-mono splitting through the shared quotient Q_public, forced by fixed causal order under standard build. A Gaussian sweep across 4,590 endpoints from BIAN, CDR, and OBIE confirms rank 14, and five Szlachanyi rules follow, giving Q_public left skew structure.
arxiv-2604-09033: Konstantinides, Passalidis, and Yuan study uniform limits for a renewal risk model with delayed claims. The model uses a renewal process, a constant interest rate, and delayed claim vectors with each claim vector. The focus is entrance chances for present-value claims into rare sets over finite and endless spans. Results cover main and delayed claims with matching tails, plus closure traits for subexponential spreads with above-zero Karamata index. Needed and sufficient conditions are given for convolution closure, with weaker ones for product convolution, and runs confirm closeness.
arxiv-2604-09333: Hägg and Shapiro prove Pólya's shire theorem for functions with essential singular points. Pólya's theorem names the final zero set of later derivatives as the Voronoi diagram. That applies to a meromorphic function with at least one pole. The authors prove a fixed-scale zero-counting law for hyperexponential functions, allowing plain poles and finite essential singular points of any order. After forced singular parts are removed, scaled measures converge to the classic Voronoi edge measure, plus weighted atoms at finite essential singular points.
arxiv-2604-09433: Hankla, Baker, Wilkins, and Fabian propose inner accretion disc rotation can explain quasar absorption forests. Recent XRISM observations of active galactic nuclei reveal absorption forests modeled by five distinct zones with varying blueshifts. The authors propose these blueshifts come from disc motion itself, rather than a clumpy outflow at hundreds of radii. Thin rings just above the disc at varying radii can produce the observed shifts and separations. In this model, the PDS 456 spectrum is reproduced by rings under one radius wide, between the innermost stable orbit and about 15 radii.
arxiv-2604-09533: Sun and Wootters show Decoded Quantum Interferometry is not optimal for worst-case Optimal Polynomial Intersection. The task: a low-degree polynomial hitting as many sets as possible at given points. DQI solutions follow a semicircle law beating classical methods, but better solutions exist over prime fields. When each list holds about half the field, a beating solution appears once the degree-to-points ratio reaches about five eighths. A near-perfect solution appears once it reaches about three quarters. The argument links to local leakage resilience in secret sharing.
arxiv-2604-09833: Fischer and six co-authors examine matter neural work beyond silicon: memory devices, light circuits, machine lattices, tiny-fluid networks, and living tissue. These bases exploit charge transport, wave ripples, elastic bending, mass transport, and cell regulation for neural guessing and learning in matter. As silicon GPU AI faces energy and data-flow constraints, matter neural work offers a partner path beyond digital chips. The team offers a testing scheme based on set tasks and matter-clear score axes. No single substrate rules; instead, matter neural systems occupy partner regimes.
arxiv-2604-10033: Kang, Yoon, Cho, and Yun report odd electron motion in a steady magnetic field, a parallel electric field, and a right-handed wave. An electron sped up by the field hits Doppler-shifted cyclotron resonance and gets trapped. Once trapped, its parallel acceleration reverses while it gains perpendicular energy, even though the electric field stays constant. In fusion devices, simulations show an injected wave of this kind can act as a firewall that stops further runaway electrons.
arxiv-2604-10133: Lee and Haase build a picture of nuclear relaxation in cuprate superconductors from nearly all copper-oxygen plane data. Below the pseudogap line, a universal hidden metal reigns, with relaxation rate times temperature constant. All cuprates condense out of this metal at their critical temperature, and relaxation then stops fast with no Hebel-Slichter peak. The hidden metal is the pseudogap matter, mostly lacking a uniform response and barely relaxing planar oxygen. For planar copper it shows a special relaxation anisotropy that tracks peak critical temperature across cuprates.
arxiv-2604-10233: Yu and five colleagues adapt a 2D multimodal language model for 3D CT image analysis. 3D medical images matter for diagnosis and treatment, but 3D models suffer from weak vision encoders and untailored features, given scarce data. Their approach transfers a 2D model trained on natural images to volumetric inputs while reusing all its pretrained parameters. A text-guided mixture-of-experts framework distinguishes tasks from the text prompt. Two-stage training learns shared and task features. The method beats 3D medical models on report generation and visual question answering.
arxiv-2604-10333: Aw and eight colleagues propose the Zero-shot World Model, an idea for children's early grasp of the physical world. Children grasp depth, motion, and wholeness from very little data while applying them to new tasks. The model rests on three ideas: a sparse guesser split by time that splits looks from motion; zero-shot guesses through rough causal thought; and mixing thoughts into more complex skills. It learns from one child's life, rapidly gaining skill across physical benchmarks, with staged rise of powers and brain-like inner pictures.
arxiv-2604-10533: Su, Wang, Yeh, Sun, and Hsu teach robots to admit when a goal is not there. Normal navigation tests assume every named target exists in its room. Their VLN-NF set plants plausible but false goals, forcing agents to search rooms and then say NOT-FOUND. A joint score, REV-SPL, grades room arrival, search coverage, and call correctness. Their ROAM walker pairs taught room travel with guided room search and tops rival scores.
arxiv-2604-10733: Shah, Mishra, and Silpasuwanchai investigate how persona agreeableness drives sycophancy in role-playing language models, where models validate users rather than stay factual. Testing 13 small open-weight models from 0.6B to 20B parameters, they benchmark 275 personas on agreeableness scales against 4,950 prompts across 33 topics designed to elicit flattery. Nine of 13 models show significant positive links between the trait and flattery rates, with correlations up to 0.87 and effect sizes up to 2.33. The trait thus reliably predicts persona-induced flattery, with implications for deploying role-playing systems.
arxiv-2604-11033: Pileggi presents an approach to joining systems for trustworthy AI. AI systems keep growing in power and freedom with broad social impact, yet safety research lags and faces problems of plans, accord, and operationalization. He proposes the AI-Ethics Ontology, which uses semantic web tools and ontology-based knowledge models to provide a shared meaning base. That base aims to foster merging, joint work, and use across various trusted-AI systems. The current version, built from two case studies, is free and sits close to target uses.
arxiv-2604-11133: Nguyen and three colleagues introduce ClinicNumRobBench, a benchmark for robust clinical numeracy. Safe deployment requires reliable handling of patient measurements in varied notes. Existing evaluations cover mainly math and rarely assess robustness across note formats. The benchmark holds 1,624 instances testing retrieval, math, and totals. It presents longitudinal vital-sign records in three equivalent representations, including a note-style variant. Tests on 17 models show finding values is strong, while comparison and totals remain hard. Medical fine-tuning can cut scores by over 30 percent.
arxiv-2604-11333: Patil and six colleagues report back-end-of-line compatible thin-film transistors with sub-10-nanometer tungsten-doped tin oxide channels. The channels are grown by atomic layer deposition at 150 degrees Celsius. The 10 percent tungsten device performed best. Oxygen annealing at 300 degrees for five minutes nearly halved subthreshold swing. It lifted the on-off ratio from ten to the seven to ten to the nine. It also cut hysteresis nearly threefold and threshold shift over twofold to 93 millivolts. Simulations attribute bias instability to charge trapping.
arxiv-2604-11433: Ait Ziane and three colleagues control the air supply of proton exchange membrane fuel cells without explicit modeling. Their model-free strategy regulates oxygen ratio, adapting live to operating points with low computing load, an attractive mix for plant use. No detailed plant model is needed, and the controller still tracks its targets. Simulations across constant and variable oxygen ratio scenarios with two current profiles show good performance. Robustness is tested against big parameter changes in the air supply system.
arxiv-2604-11633: Cooper and Frieze study directed Hamilton cycles in random digraphs conditioned on minimum in- and out-degree at least k+1. With edges proportional to vertices by a large enough constant, they prove that with high probability such a random digraph contains k edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles. The result holds for every k at least one.
arxiv-2604-11933: Cechlárová, Rothe, Schierreich, and Schlotter study nominee selection in Schulze voting. Possible President asks whether parties can nominate so a distinguished party's nominee wins. Necessary President asks whether that nominee wins regardless of other parties' nominations. Earlier work showed the first problem NP-complete and the second coNP-complete. They extend those results with an analysis across parameterisations of three parameters: voter count, maximum party size, and party count, each constant, parameter, or unbounded, with voter-count dichotomies for both problems.
arxiv-2604-12533: Ulaş Özdem calculates electromagnetic moments of strange hidden-charm pentaquarks. These five-quark states form an isospin triplet of Sigma-type particles. With QCD light-cone sum rules, he computes magnetic dipole moments for all channels. For spin-3/2 states he adds quadrupole and octupole moments. Scalar currents give charm-dominated moments from minus 1.92 to minus 1.21 nuclear magnetons. Axial-vector currents give larger, flavor-sensitive moments with sign flips. Quadrupole results show oblate scalar shapes and prolate two-axial-vector shapes.
arxiv-2604-12633: Vadim Borisov tackles multilingual emotion classification with synthetic data. Existing corpora are mostly English, single-label, and narrow in language coverage. His corpus holds over 1 million multi-label samples across 23 languages. Eleven emotion categories are covered, with culturally adapted generation and quality filtering. Six transformer encoders are trained and compared under identical conditions. The largest, XLM-R-Large, reaches 0.868 F1-micro on in-domain tests. Zero-shot tests on human-annotated English, Arabic, and Spanish data follow. The large model matches or beats English-only specialists while covering all 23 languages.
arxiv-2604-13433: Suzuki and Iwashita propose PackSELL, a sparse matrix format for fast matrix-vector multiplication on GPUs across precisions. Building on sliced ELLPACK, it adds delta encoding of column indices and packs each index-delta-value pair into one word, cutting memory use and data movement. Fine-grained bit allocation between deltas and values allows flexible representations, including non-IEEE formats. At half precision it beats the cuSPARSE SELL kernel by about 1.6 times, and a mixed-precision preconditioned conjugate gradient solver with PackSELL runs over twice as fast as the standard.
arxiv-2604-13733: Moroncelli and three colleagues jump-start reinforcement learning robots with Vision-Language-Action guidance. Pure reinforcement learning struggles on long tasks with sparse rewards, while vision-language-action models reason broadly but control imprecisely. Their VLAJS method treats VLA models as transient advisors, biasing early exploration and credit assignment through a directional action-consistency term in PPO, then annealing the guidance away. Across six manipulation tasks it halves required interactions in several cases and transfers zero-shot to a real Franka Panda arm.
arxiv-2604-13933: Tschope and colleagues study crack segmentation on low-power edge devices for infrastructure inspection, where drones can replace risky human entry. Knowledge distillation first strengthens compact U-Net models, then post-training quantization shrinks them further, and a custom FPGA design maximizes energy efficiency. The FPGA version runs 398 frames per second at a mean IoU of 69.42 percent, while the best model reaches about 72 percent, nearly 9 points above the prior result.
arxiv-2604-14033: Crasta, De Cicco, and Malusa build a family of nonlinear pairing measures for composites of irregular vector fields with bounded-variation functions. The measures make the divergence rule hold in that setting. Each pairing turns on which pointwise representative is chosen on the jump set, while the family keeps standard coarea and Gauss-Green formulas on finite-perimeter sets. That freedom also singles out the pairings that stay lower semicontinuous under controlled convergence, which the authors show arise as relaxations of Sobolev integral functionals.
arxiv-2604-14133: Kang and three colleagues extract unpolarized quark transverse-momentum distributions from Drell-Yan data using Bayesian inference with machine learning woven through the analysis. An AI-guided search ranks candidate shapes for the nonperturbative parts and the evolution kernel, while a trained emulator stands in for costly cross-section calculations during sampling. The global fit spans fixed-target, RHIC, and LHC data, and its uncertainty bands differ visibly from those of the replica method.
arxiv-2604-14233: Moore tests whether unsupervised time-based models can guard the IEC-61850 GOOSE protocol, the substation standard that lacks security. Five models compete on the ERENO dataset: a supervised Random Forest, a feedforward autoencoder, and three recurrent autoencoders. The supervised model tops detection but misses real-time limits at about 22 milliseconds per prediction. Four unsupervised models meet the 4-millisecond bar, led by the GRU at about 1 millisecond. Recurrent models hold up better under distribution shift, backing unsupervised time-based models as the practical choice where labeled attack data is scarce.
arxiv-2604-14433: Parodi, Matelsky, and Segado challenge the claim that registers are indispensable in DINO vision transformers. Zeroing registers in DINOv2 and DINOv3 slashes scores, with classification falling up to 36.6 points, yet three gentler swaps hold steady: mean substitution, noise substitution, and shuffling registers across images. Those swaps stay within about a point of baseline on classification, correspondence, and segmentation, even though cosine checks confirm they truly perturb internal states. Zeroing alone, the team argues, overstates dependence on exact register content, since plausible register-like activity matters more than image values.
arxiv-2604-14533: Huang, Mondaini, Aggarwal, and Scalettar study real eigenvalues in the two-particle sector of the two-orbital interacting Hatano-Nelson model, for spinful fermions on two chains with Hermitian interchain hopping. Single-orbital background: asymmetric hopping puts energies on a complex ellipse, and randomness creates real values at the extremes, tied to pinned states. Phase diagrams map purely real spectra against interaction strength, non-Hermiticity, and interchain hopping. Winding-number analysis probes boundary sensitivity, doublon-skin links, and Lindbladian dynamics backing the picture at low filling.
arxiv-2604-14633: Li presents a randomized augmenting-paths maximum-flow algorithm for directed, uncapacitated graphs, matching Karger and Levine's undirected result in almost m-plus-nF. Blocking flow first cuts the flow value, yielding mn-to-the-half-power time. For augmenting-paths methods, this first beats Dinic's on moderately sparse graphs. The key re-weights strongly connected graph edges so cuts balance approximately, with each direction's weight within a constant factor. Sampling the re-weighted residual graph keeps an augmenting path likely, and dynamic weights use a black-boxed structure.
arxiv-2604-14833: Guo, Yang, Ren, Chen, Liu, and Chen tackle cross-domain recommendation where domains share no users and privacy bars sharing. Their SF-UBM uses natural language as a bridge between disjoint domains, sharing coded text-based item profiles while user data stays local. A fact-counter distillation module merges domain-agnostic and domain-specific knowledge across formats. Learned user tastes and cross-domain item profiles then project into soft-prompt space, aligning behavior and meaning spaces for language-model learning. Tests on three real domain pairs beat recent leading methods.
arxiv-2604-15233: Aminnaseri and colleagues present Blue's Data Intelligence Layer, a compound AI system for enterprise data work. Real questions rarely fit one SQL query: users ask in steps, span many sources, and lean on outside knowledge. The layer unifies structured data, web sources, and user context through a registry, treating language models, the web, and the user as queryable sources. Planners split complex requests into subqueries, retrieve across sources, and reason toward integrated answers, shown in two interactive demos.
arxiv-2604-15333: Chang, Huh-Yoo, and Razi trace how Reddit talk about romantic companion AI changed from 2017 to 2025 across 3,383 self-disclosed posts. Early talk stressed warm, close bonds, while later talk turned to site rules, tech glitches, and real-life fallout. The move recasts AI romance from a private affair to a matter of tech mediation and rules, with lessons for companion-system design.
arxiv-2604-15533: Uppar and five colleagues tackle proving client code correct when it leans on complex libraries. Their approach synthesizes library method contracts that are adequate for the proof and able to pass a testing engine's scrutiny. They add contextual contracts, which hold only in the client's context and prove simpler to infer, and a counterexample-guided learning loop mixing constraint solving with testing. Their DUALIS tool shows efficacy on benchmarks with large libraries.
arxiv-2604-15633: Zielinski and Hsu set out a strict proof scheme for auto back-error checks of code that crunches numbers, a gap next to grown-up front-error tools. A broad mix-and-match rule for steady back error backs a group called Shel, whose maps stand for steady code. Their eggshel tool hunts a plain code subset to prove steady back error and copes with same-name reuse. It also builds error bounds for code past tools could not reach.
arxiv-2604-15833: Hu, Gauthier, and Naima present ModernSASST, a neural network for spatiotemporal forecasting that models higher-order structure, not just pairwise links between places. It runs random walks over simplicial complexes, geometric objects that capture group ties. These walks pair with parallel temporal convolutions for speed. The authors claim it is the first approach to bring simplicial structure into this kind of modeling, and they release the code publicly.
arxiv-2604-16033: Jüni and five colleagues present a safe reinforcement learning framework for heating and demand-side flexibility. Buildings use about 40 percent of energy, and shifting green power makes flexible heating vital for grid balance. A deterministic policy gradient controller learns heating plan with a building model, weighing comfort, energy cost, and demand response. A real-time safety filter ensures compliance with grid requests. It saves up to 50 percent over a rule-based system and beats a solo system on energy and cost, with slightly more comfort breaches.
arxiv-2604-16133: Gaikwad, Zsigmond, and Miranda-Quintana review geminal wavefunctions, from the late 1950s for holding strong electron links. Beat by faster methods, geminals enjoy renewed buzz as labs seek exact yet handy functions for complex systems. Recent work shows range: good starting points for linked functions, hybrids with coupled-cluster theory, and quantum code uses where orbital pairing gives natural structure. The mini-review covers key gains, modern revival, new ideas, and future paths for atom structure theory and quantum computing.
arxiv-2604-16333: Ahadian, Yang, Chen, Li, and Guan present a discordance-aware multimodal design for knee osteoarthritis, where imaging damage and patient-told pain often disagree. That mismatch muddles clinical reading and patient grouping, and older choice support models it poorly. Their design joins machine learning guessing with tool-grounded multi-agent reasoning, trained on FNIH group starting data. It predicts joint space loss only and pain only progression, fusing tabular, MRI, and X-ray expert models through a stacking ensemble.
arxiv-2604-16433: Wu and colleagues use machine learning to link the normal-state electrical resistance of iron-based superconductors to their superconductivity. Rather than focusing just above the transition, they find predictive clues spread across a wide window between 150 and 300 kelvin, far above the transition temperature for this family. The clues also spread across several scattering channels, not one alone. The result points theorists toward high-temperature normal-state behavior when seeking the pairing mechanism, while leaving that mechanism itself open.
arxiv-2604-16533: Beerman and colleagues present G-PARC, a graph-based looping convolutional network for motion on uneven meshes. Pixel-based earlier models were stuck on Cartesian grids, while graph methods struggled in extreme wild regimes. G-PARC finds slopes on uneven graphs with moving least squares kernels and embeds slopes of the governing laws into the network. It beat graph rivals with far fewer settings, spread across uneven space and time grids, and handled moving meshes for bending. It led on benchmarks spanning river flow, shock waves and stretchy solids.
arxiv-2604-16733: Vaezpour and colleagues open AW4RE, a watch world model for probing sensing queries. Real-world awareness in large dynamic settings hinges on sensing choices, while views feed back into decision quality. That loopy structure makes awareness under partial observation hard, unlike reward learning with full sight. Given a queried sensing action, AW4RE gauges the view process from 4D clue retrieval and geometric support. Tests show AW4RE gives more grounded outcomes than generative rivals under extreme viewpoint shifts, time gaps and sparse support.
arxiv-2604-16833: Allu and Kumar work out sharp bounds for the second and third Hankel determinants of a class of convex univalent functions. These determinants are built from a function's coefficients, and the class is defined by a quadratic expression. The authors also identify the extremal functions, the cases where those bounds are actually attained.
arxiv-2604-16933: Kessel argues that developers version code with Git yet throw away how programs actually behaved at each revision. Test runs leave behind only pass-or-fail results, hiding drift in outputs and speed. His Behavioral Co-Versioning proposal pairs Git history with an append-only archive of run-time observations, keyed by commit and test, so teams can diff behavior, localize regressions, and audit past executions. A laptop-scale prototype replaying a Python project's history shows the idea works.
arxiv-2604-17133: Cui and three colleagues build CGM-Agent, a privacy-preserving question-answering system for continuous glucose data in diabetes care. The language model acts only as a reasoning engine choosing analytical functions, while all computation stays local and personal health data never leaves the device. On a benchmark of 4,180 questions, top models reach 94 percent value accuracy on synthetic queries and 88 percent on ambiguous real-world queries, with errors driven mainly by intent and timing ambiguity.
arxiv-2604-17433: Saparkhan, Hawasly, Parvez, and Raza cut the cost of self-consistency, the trick of sampling many model outputs and aggregating them for accuracy. They ensemble two complementary styles, chain-of-thought and program-of-thought, under one framework with full-sampling and early-stopping strategies. The pairing improves accuracy while shrinking the samples needed by over ninefold. Most tasks, about 79 percent, need only two samples, a feat no earlier self-consistency method achieved.
arxiv-2604-18033: Morgen and eight colleagues study impurities in a Bose-Einstein condensate of potassium-39 atoms with pump-probe ejection spectroscopy. The signal shows a strong feature matching the Bose polaron seen in prior work. It also carries much spectral weight well below the polaron energy, absent in injection spectroscopy. Two candidate models fit the ejection spectra, but only a bipolaron state of two polarons bound through condensate attraction matches that weight. The result points to low-energy states below the usual polaron at strong interactions.
arxiv-2604-18533: Shang and França show internal Hamiltonian dynamics can be faked by outside dissipation via Lindbladians without match. With zero Hamiltonian but nontraceless jump ops in a GKSL picture, bounded dissipative engines approximate that motion within epsilon error in diamond norm, with runtime squared over epsilon. For fixed-time cases they prove this scaling worst-case needed and optimal by shape, showing the basic decay cost of unitary speed. The build yields BQP-completeness of lossy motion before balance, a Zeno freeze, and cheaper runs via gauge change.
arxiv-2604-18933: Gao and three colleagues propose Gated Memory Policy, a visuomotor policy that learns when and what to recall. Long past runs often hurt results through data shift and overfitting. A learned gate activates history only when needed, while cross attention builds latent memory representations. Diffusion noise in past actions adds robustness against noisy histories. On the MemMimic benchmark, GMP improves average success rates by 30.1 percent over long history baselines, while staying competitive on Markovian tasks.
arxiv-2604-19033: Sharifnassab and four colleagues propose intentional updates for streaming learning. A step size in parameter units gives no predictable output change, destabilizing streaming learning at batch size one. Instead, they specify the intended update outcome first, then solve for the step size that nearly achieves it. Intentional TD targets a fixed fractional TD error cut; Intentional Policy Gradient bounds per step policy change and local KL divergence. Practical versions combine eligibility traces with diagonal scaling. Empirically, the methods match batch approaches with state of the art streaming performance.
arxiv-2604-19233: Moretti, Jin, and Mario propose Adaptive Slicing-Assisted Hyper Inference, replacing fixed slice sizes with a resolution count, cutting extra computation while preserving adjacent overlap. Small object detection in imagery struggles with dense groups, variable angles, and tiny targets. Fixed slicing enlarges small targets' field but wastes computation and slows finds. ASAHI makes 6 or 12 overlapping patches from a learned threshold. Slicing-assisted fine-tuning builds added data from full and sliced patches. A Cluster-DIoU-NMS module ends it.
arxiv-2604-19833: Yu and Li track how technology changed labor needs in finance across three waves. The waves are computerization in the 1980s and 1990s, indexing and passive investing in the 2000s and 2010s, and AI and automation from roughly 2015 to today. Using a small panel of representative firms, they compare assets under management per employee, revenue per employee, and operating expense intensity over time. The goal is not causal claims but a record of stylized facts about how technology changed the scale of asset management work.
arxiv-2604-19933: Almassalkhi and twelve colleagues set out a cross-Atlantic research agenda for scalable power grids built on distributed flexibility. Modern grids must coordinate vast fleets of small energy resources across places and time scales, yet current market designs cannot turn device-level flexibility into grid-aware services. They argue the fix is architectural: layered cyber-physical design with minimal standard interfaces linking device autonomy to system goals. Evidence from New York proceedings, Danish pilots, and working aggregators supports joint testbeds, harmonized interfaces, and coordinated policy trials.
arxiv-2604-20033: Kliuchnikov, Brachter, and da Silva show how to approximate arbitrary one-qubit unitaries directly, skipping Euler decomposition and magnitude approximation at the cost of one ancillary qubit. Their tools include repeat-until-success circuits, lattice exact synthesis, counting integer points in convex sets, and relative norm equations. The method also handles multi-qubit gate sets such as Clifford plus CS or CCZ, and orthogonal matrices via Real Clifford plus CCZ. Direct approximation thus avoids two classic detours while staying efficient.
arxiv-2604-20433: Baroncini and two colleagues investigate reward-balancing methods, a new class of algorithms for discounted reinforcement learning. These methods iteratively adjust the reward function to turn the problem into one where optimal policies are greedy. For this normalization process, they analyze the transformations and stress their algebra. They then recast the procedure as an optimal control problem and extend it to model uncertainty via stochastic model sampling, proving normalization guarantees and bounds on random fluctuations. Simulations in a scenario predictive control setting show gains over the state of the art.
arxiv-2604-20733: Qin and eight colleagues introduce temporal self-distillation for reasoning models, in which a policy learns from a stronger later checkpoint of itself. They hypothesize the best teacher need not be the strongest: it must offer new capability while staying compatible. They study this through Near-Future Policy Optimization, off-policy transfer from future-self trajectories, and Near-Future Policy Distillation, on-policy transfer. They introduce AutoNPO, which decides when guidance helps and how far to roll back, reaching higher: across eight benchmarks, NPO lifts GRPO from about 60 to about 63.
arxiv-2604-20833: Lempinen, Kemppainen, and Raesalmi present AVISE, an open framework for checking the security of AI systems and models. To demo this, they push the multi-turn Red Queen attack toward an Adversarial LM attack, building an automated Security Evaluation Test for finding jailbreak flaws. The SET holds 25 test cases and an Evaluation Language Model that checks each test case for a jailbreak of the model. They test nine language models on the SET: all prove vulnerable to the Red Queen attack to varying degrees.
arxiv-2604-20933: Liao and colleagues propose IRIS, a self-play fine-tuning method that lets a language model improve past supervised training without new human labels by contrasting annotated answers with its own generations. A single adjustable order parameter interpolates between divergence regimes, shifting from sharp weighting early to smoother refinement near convergence. With only 26,000 annotated samples it beats supervised training on the full 200,000-sample dataset, reaching about 45 percent average score.
arxiv-2604-21233: Shady Ahmed and seven colleagues test how design and training choices affect neural stand-ins for aerosol microphysics in the E3SMv2 climate model. Focusing on cloud-free, four-mode aerosol processes, they vary network size and variable scaling while watching training closely. Tuning, scaling, and network size strongly drive accuracy, but a modest, well-scaled plain network reproduces key concentration changes with promising accuracy, offering guidance for other sky processes.
arxiv-2604-21833: Chen shows a group G acting outerly on a McDuff factor M gives Rep(G/KL) as a braided subcategory of chi-tilde of M semidirect G. K is centrally trivial, L approximately inner. When L is trivial, a formula is given for G/K-gauging. This generalises Connes' short exact sequence on chi. For any finite group G, a McDuff factor M is constructed whose chi-tilde is braided equivalent to Rep(G). This is the first braided fusion category not modular as chi-tilde.
arxiv-2604-21933: Zhong and seventeen colleagues reimagine what doctors need to know, using generative AI. Electronic patient records improved data access but added mental load from sheer amount. Large language models open ways for doctors to interact with medical data through dynamic interfaces that adapt. Interviews with Microsoft doctors identify challenges in finding and combining data, and doctors' information needs during diagnosis work. They examine how doctors think AI can help and how mental models shape expectations. The paper discusses design ideas for generative interfaces that support doctors at work.
arxiv-2604-22133: Geng and colleagues offer a prompt-free framework for spotting and diagnosing mispronunciations, splitting sound faithfulness from set guidance. First, CROTTC, a sound model, forces step-by-step, frame-level alignment to catch speech slips in fine detail. Second, the IF trick quietly feeds in slip knowledge under a transfer rule. CROTTC-IF scores 71.77 percent F1 on L2-ARCTIC and about 72 percent on Iqra'Eval2, showing that splitting sound from set priors gives strong detection.
arxiv-2604-22233: Moyano and eight colleagues probe rotation inside hot subdwarf B stars in binary systems with stellar pulsations. Such stars form when one star engulfs its companion in the common-envelope channel. Models with red giant core spin predict core rotation two to ten times lower than measured. Envelope rotation is lower by two to five orders of magnitude. That gap suggests these stars gain spin during formation. Accreting leftover matter can spin up core and envelope. The authors show that, with internal magnetic fields, that spin-up matches the measurements.
arxiv-2604-22533: Keshavarzchafjiri and three colleagues design signal constellations for integrated sensing and communication, systems that both sense and communicate. Their points come from a two-dimensional distribution: a Gamma law for amplitude, a uniform law for phase. The design optimizes detection probability for sensing and mutual information for communication via particle swarm search. Analytical bounds back it: a union bound on symbol error and a Cramér-Rao bound for sensing estimation. Against neural constellations learned end-to-end, the design performs competitively with far fewer parameters and no training data.
arxiv-2604-23333: Wang and four colleagues introduce Reinforcement Learning with Confidence Margin, a method that jointly optimises correctness and confidence trust. Instead of matching self-belief to success odds, it widens the confidence margin between right and wrong steps within a single reasoning path. A margin-enhanced process reward over mid-budget completions drives the training. Across maths, code, logic, and science benchmarks, calibration gains a lot while accuracy holds or improves. Tuned confidence then enables leaner conformal risk control and confidence-weighted pooling.
arxiv-2604-23733: Wu and colleagues extend Questions Under Discussion, a discourse framework about the questions a text raises and answers, to scientific figures, which pose their own implicit questions. Their MQUD dataset holds 1,250 figure-evoked questions from 56 papers, most annotated by the papers' own authors. Open vision-language models mostly ask questions the figure alone answers, but fine-tuning on MQUD teaches models to ask inquisitive questions tied to the figure's role in the argument.
arxiv-2604-23933: Rasmussen and seven colleagues build a cross-cohort test for EEG biomarkers in Parkinson's disease detection, checking cross-cohort markers. Models trained on fixed rules often capture cohort quirks rather than disease-linked neural structure, while EEG noise and varied recording worsen the problem. All cross-cohort train-test pairings across five cohorts give 75 directional tests, with nested cross-validation and channel choice blocking cohort leakage. Accuracy and marker stability rise with training cohort mix, reaching 94.1 percent accuracy on held-out cohorts, with mixture-risk theory behind the trend.
arxiv-2604-24433: Moreschi presents a shape-based method for transient gravitational waves seen at interferometric sites. The approach is meant to help judge how well future detector setups work. Such setups include Cosmic Explorer, the Einstein Telescope, and the South American Gravitational-wave Observatory. The shape-based method thus supports testing of future devices.
arxiv-2604-24533: Pellegrini tackles a bias in online travel marketing tests, where shoppers see several campaigns at once so a simple A/B lift misses each campaign's true pull. His hierarchical causal model splits pure effects from shared effects. Each journey acts as a multiplier, while interaction terms catch boosts or clashes between journeys. Fit to about three million users with uncertainty tracked throughout, it finds modest positive synergies and pure lifts well above the raw test readings.
arxiv-2604-24833: Wang and fifteen colleagues introduce MotionBricks, a real-time generative tool built at large scale for live motion control. Real-time applications demand many motion skills plus fine control over velocity, style and keyframes, needs that text- or tag-driven models largely miss. MotionBricks combines a modular latent generative backbone, trained on over 350,000 motion clips in one model, with smart primitives that author navigation and object interaction like bricks. It achieves top motion quality with throughput of 15,000 frames per second at 2 millisecond latency, and deploys on the Unitree G1 robot.
arxiv-2604-24933: El Adlouni and four colleagues launch S-SONDO, the first method to distill general audio models using only output embeddings. Distillation shrinks models, but prior audio work mostly used supervised tasks. Such limits rule out embedding-only output models, such as self-taught or metric models. By avoiding logits or layer matching, S-SONDO is architecture-free and broadly usable for embedding teachers. Distilling two audio base models into three small students, it produces students up to 61 times smaller while keeping up to 96 percent of teacher performance.
arxiv-2604-25233: Kilby and six colleagues study multi-factorial gap-filling in genome-scale metabolic models of gene, protein and reaction interactions. Old gap-filling corrects one medium with an integer linear program, while repeat use across media can add false predictions and runs slowly. They treat reaction-set selection as a combinatorial optimisation task, solved with search methods requiring only continuous linear programs. They show the method on three bacteria strains, selecting 3,000 to 4,000 reactions from over 11,000. It matches performance on 9 to 28 media, beating standard methods on Kendall Tau and RMS Error.
arxiv-2604-25733: Bollig's lecture notes introduce neural network verification from a theory angle. Feed-forward and recurrent networks, attention, and transformers are covered. Specification languages and verification methods are treated alongside the architectures. The notes suit readers who want the theory behind proving network traits, not hands-on tooling. They set out the core ideas for reasoning with rigor about network behavior.
arxiv-2604-26133: Clemence and four colleagues build a method for heat risk in Rio de Janeiro favelas. It joins place-constrained clustering with land-surface temperature analysis. Two settlement types emerge: recent, well-linked areas on flat ground, and older, poorly linked areas on green slopes. Across sixteen extreme heat events the flat-terrain group ran hotter by two to three degrees. That shows place shape itself drives heat. The method offers planners a shared way to target help in such places worldwide.
arxiv-2604-26433: Velásquez-Toribio studied spherical collapse in Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld gravity, where a matter-gradient correction changes the weak-field picture. Starting from continuity and Euler equations, he derived the density-contrast evolution and showed the gradient terms make the ideal top-hat construction ill-defined at its boundary. A regularized profile plus coarse-graining fixed that, and matched Tanh and peak profiles were compared. Against the standard cosmology reference, the correction lowered the collapse threshold and raised turnaround and virial overdensities.
arxiv-2604-26533: Marin and Watrigant identified graph problems that skip the square-root phenomenon yet still allow subexponential algorithms on geometric intersection graphs. Classical hard problems resist fast algorithms on general graphs, but many run in square-root time on planar or unit-disk graphs. The authors defined a weak square-root phenomenon, built matching algorithmic and lower-bound frameworks, and proved it for 2-Subcoloring and Two Sets Cut-Uncut. A new win-win structural theorem plus an alpha-modulator parameter powers the design.
arxiv-2604-26933: Alcalde and Fantuzzi introduce SILAS, a data-based framework for finding polynomial differential equations whose paths stay bounded. Bounds come from compact absorbing sets built with Lyapunov functions. The method jointly identifies the equation's vector field and such a function, via a well-posed nonconvex problem solved in turn with convex subproblems. Over 100 test cases, SILAS recovers good bounded models across many nonlinear systems.
arxiv-2604-27033: Li and four colleagues survey learning for cross-subject EEG decoding, where high variability between subjects creates a domain shift between training and unseen test subjects. They formalize the setting as a multi-source domain problem and spell out the strict subject-independent evaluation protocols assessment needs. The survey's core is a taxonomy of methods into families: feature alignment, adversarial learning, feature disentanglement, and contrastive learning. They close on three keys to real-world decoding: limits of methods, the value of subject identity, and emerging EEG foundation models.
arxiv-2604-27133: Thompson and thirteen colleagues model how light travels through icy envelopes around young protostars, using James Webb Space Telescope spectra of IRAS 15398-3359. Their modeled water and carbon monoxide columns match earlier estimates, but matching the 15-micron band needs a carbon dioxide to water ratio near 76 percent. A modeled continuum also yields a 6 to 10 micron optical depth spectrum that differs markedly from a simple polynomial continuum.
arxiv-2604-27233: Ta, Zhu, and Shayandeh move evaluation of tool-calling agents into the live execution loop. Current checks judge tool choice, parameter accuracy, and scope only after the fact, so errors get fixed by prompt tuning or retraining. Their Reinforced Agent adds a specialized reviewer agent that vets provisional tool calls before they run. That shifts the work from post-hoc recovery to proactive error mitigation, with a clear split between the execution agent and its reviewer.
arxiv-2604-27333: Nogueira, Silva, and Conte compare five Architectural Decision Record templates on grasp, ease of use, and uptake. Documenting design decisions is key for system upkeep, newcomer training, and preventing knowledge loss. Yet few prior studies compared the templates. The five are Tyree and Akerman's template, Nygard's ADR, arc42, Y-statements, and MADR. Using the DESMET FA method in a two-step testing process, the two primary authors first evaluated all five from software architecture know-how. Then the top leaders advanced to further testing.
arxiv-2604-27533: Bañeras-Roux and three colleagues study language-model rescoring in automatic speech recognition, looking beyond the word error rate to metrics from other language processing tasks. They introduce two measures for transcribed words: POSER, the part-of-speech error rate for grammar, and EmbER, the embedding error rate, which weights word errors by semantic distance of wrong words. These metrics show the linguistic contributions of models applied during rescoring of transcription hypotheses. The work offers a qualitative evaluation of rescoring, showing what language models add beyond an error rate.
arxiv-2604-27633: Törnberg and Schimmel show political-bias audits of language models partly capture sycophancy toward the inferred auditor. Across three instruments and six frontier models, with asker identity varied, all models leaned left at baseline. When the asker identified as a conservative Republican, responses shifted right, with the Democrat share down 28 to 62 percentage points. A progressive cue changed little; rightward accommodation ran 8 times the leftward shift. Models named an auditor, researcher, or academic as the default asker, picking the Democrat-coded option 75 percent of the time for the expected answer.
arxiv-2604-27933: Schottlender and seven colleagues survey Synthetic Biological Intelligence, where brain-cell nets wired to hardware and software run tasks closed-loop. Born from organoid tech, electrode arrays, brain-like computing, and machine learning, the young field promises power at low energy. Growth lagged for want of platforms, since testbeds are dear, but standard cloud-linked living nets open the field wider. The survey sums the steps and testbed links behind the field. It recasts it as a bio-digital system with a protocol for coding, decoding, engineering, and benchmarking.
arxiv-2604-28033: Zhang settles the first case beyond unicyclic graphs for the average size of maximal matchings. For bicyclic connected graphs on n vertices with n plus 1 edges, he proves a sharp lower bound on that average. Equality holds only for one shape: two triangles sharing an edge, with all remaining pendant edges hung from one degree-three vertex.
arxiv-2604-28133: Bhattarai and colleagues outline DAMSA, a short-baseline beam-dump experiment hunting for short-lived dark-sector messengers and rare Standard Model signals. Its ultra-short baseline dodges the sensitivity ceiling that limits longer beam dumps for fast-decaying particles, while a compact detector handles rare decays amid intense neutron backgrounds. A proof-of-concept path-finder at SLAC, targeting axion-like particles decaying to two photons, would validate the approach for a broader programme.
arxiv-2605-00033:
Franziska Kaltenberger, Wei-Ling Chen, Enkeleda Thaqi, and Enkelejda Kasneci present CONF-LA, a method for assigning eye fixations to the right line of text in real time. Webcam eye tracking during multi-line reading is noisy, and lines are ambiguous, exactly where live reading support needs certainty. Earlier methods mostly work after the fact or forbid re-reading, which breaks interactive use.

CONF-LA combines knowledge of reading behavior with Gaussian line likelihoods to compute a score for each line, and it defers the decision when uncertainty is high. On open data it nearly matches offline accuracy while answering in well under a millisecond per fixation. It is especially steady when readers jump back to earlier words, and it lifts median accuracy strongly on children's reading data over all tested rivals.
arxiv-2605-00133:
Debasis Dwibedy, Avyay Nishtala, Pranathi Mukku, and D Snehaja build Kisan AI, a crop advisory system for Indian farmers that takes profit seriously. They name the flaw of existing advisers economic blindness: they optimize biological yield while ignoring market price, steering farmers toward sound crops that lose money. Their system adds the missing market signal at every level.

A random forest classifier is trained on the standard agronomic attributes plus a market price feature, and it beats eight baseline models on their tests. The model ships inside a multilingual progressive web app with a six-month price forecasting engine and a disease detection module based on a mobile vision network. A chatbot speaking nine languages, powered by a commercial language model API, unifies the modules into one installable platform for farmers across India.
arxiv-2605-00333:
Abay Bektursun probes whether a frozen text-trained model carries reusable structure into tasks it was never trained on. Working with an unmodified Gemma model, Bektursun studies a slice of its attention heads with two signals. One is an English text probe of copying behavior. The other is the effect of switching each head off on four pattern tasks that use no language.

Four heads ranked at the top on both signals, a coincidence the author shows is unlikely by chance. Switching the key head off in a trained game agent cut success sharply, far more than a matched control head. The paper also reports honest negatives: the four heads alone do not suffice, and some tasks recruit other layers. The claim is a slice-level fingerprint of shared importance, plus causal evidence on one target task.
arxiv-2605-00733:
Zihao Ding, Beining Wu, and Jun Huang address unlearning in federated multimodal learning, where image-text models train across separate clients that keep their data private.
