Joint training entangles knowledge to be forgotten across both modalities and across client update directions, so simple removal fails. Forgotten alignments can survive through cross-modal links, shared subspaces, and later federated updates.

Their EASE framework attacks all three residual anchors. It displaces both visual and language branches to close the reconstruction channel, separates forget-only directions from retained ones using a Cosine-Sine decomposition, and locks against drift across rounds. Across datasets and scenarios, EASE stays close to the retrain reference on both forgotten and retained data.
arxiv-2605-00833:
Brice Valentin Kok-Shun, Johnny Chan, Gabrielle Peko, and David Sundaram present Agentopic, a workflow that uses several language-model agents together for topic modeling with explanations. Standard tools such as LDA and BERTopic can group documents well, but they rarely show why a topic was assigned or grouped. Agentopic splits the work among agents that find topics, validate them, group them in a hierarchy, and explain them in plain language.

Seeded with topics from a BBC dataset, Agentopic matches a strong language model on accuracy and sits close to BERTopic. Without seeding, it produced more than two thousand coherent topics across six levels, far richer than the original five categories. The authors highlight uses in finance and health care.
arxiv-2605-01033:
Taras Krokhmalskii and five co-authors examine how an electromagnetic wave travels through a one-dimensional magnetic crystal, modeled as a quantum spin chain. By calculating the dispersion relation, which links wave frequency to wave number, they illustrate how an external magnetic field can control the spread of the wave through the medium. The model is deliberately simple, so the calculations can be done rigorously.

The authors argue those rigorous results should be useful for more realistic models of magnetic media that are less tractable mathematically. Readers get a clear baseline for how field-tunable magnetic structure changes wave propagation, with exact relations against which approximate treatments of richer materials can be checked.
arxiv-2605-01233:
Xiaokang Li and four co-authors present a study testing whether quantum entanglement in tau lepton pairs can be probed at the planned Super Tau-Charm Facility. Bell-inequality violation in such pairs offers a sensitive probe of quantum correlations in high-energy interactions. The study uses full Monte Carlo runs of electron-positron collisions producing tau pairs, focusing on the pion-pion decay channel.

That channel offers maximal spin-reading power and the simplest final-state topology for validating quantum tomography. A consistency chain runs from tree-level theory prediction through truth-level and detector-level reconstruction. It yields a measured concurrence with small uncertainty under a good-solution approach. A complementary study of another channel is briefly reported, supporting it as a competitive platform.
arxiv-2605-01433:
Hyunho Cha and Jungwoo Lee speed up a running estimate of entanglement witnesses that can be read from classical shadows, cheap snapshots of a quantum state. The witnesses are partial-transpose moments, prized because they can certify mixed-state entanglement and flag phase changes.

An earlier online scheme kept memory fixed by updating a few stored matrices per snapshot. But it treated each new snapshot as a solid block, so cost grew with the cube of the state space size. The pair show the update can be done exactly in less time by using the snapshot's own structure: it still splits into local factors even though the stored matrices do not. Sweeping column pairs applies the update exactly, and the second moment gets a further shortcut in the Pauli basis. Memory stays the same while each shot costs far less arithmetic.
arxiv-2605-01533:
Jia Li, Mehrdad Sabetzadeh, and Shiva Nejati teach microservice systems to scale themselves before trouble hits. Modern software is split into small services, and each needs the right number of copies running. Too few and service goals break, too many and money burns, while reactive scaling always arrives late.

Their framework, AutoSLO, closes a loop of monitoring and adaptation, and uses genetic programming to learn and evolve the scaling rules themselves. The deployed system thus carries its own scaling logic and acts ahead of violations instead of searching for a fix each time. Two case studies, an online shop and a chatbot built on a large language model, test the setup. Resource use falls substantially, service-goal violations stay rare, and every breach that does occur is cleared within a short window.
arxiv-2605-01833:
Szymon Kobus and Deniz Gündüz study remote control when the actors doing the work cannot see the reward and must be steered over a link with very little room for data. Sending full actions is costly, and the cost grows for large or smooth action spaces. Their paper sets out a way to guide learning and control while sending far less.

Instead of full actions, the controller sends small cues that let each actor sample an action from the controller's changing target policy. Actors also learn from those cues, so their local sampling improves and later messages can be smaller still. The method, called GRASP, cut data use about twelvefold on average in their tests.
arxiv-2605-01933:
Jianfeng Lu proves a sharp rate for how fast underdamped Langevin dynamics settles toward its steady state. The dynamics models a particle moving with friction and noise, widely used for sampling. Lu assumes the position part of the target satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality and that the potential is convex with suitable growth.

He builds a modified entropy that adds a correction term based on optimal transport between the current position law and the target. For a friction choice tied to the log-Sobolev constant, he obtains an explicit decay estimate from any start with finite relative entropy. The result tightens how hypocoercivity, the spread of damping through the system, can be quantified in this setting.
arxiv-2605-02033:
H M Sazzad Quadir, Sakib Al Hasan, and Md Nurul Ahad Tawhid test whether language models can label commit messages by the conventional commits format without any training. That format improves readability, maintenance, and tools such as changelog makers. Past classifiers needed large labelled sets and task-specific models, which the authors aim to avoid.

They try zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompts on three open models of different sizes, using code diffs from 3,200 balanced commits in the InfluxDB project. Few-shot prompting gave the highest accuracy overall. Chain-of-thought results are compared in the paper. The study shows prompt design alone can carry much of the classification task.
arxiv-2605-02333:
Jingwen Fu, Ming Xiao, and Mikael Skoglund split language model semantic communication into separate skills, so each part can be controlled or replaced. Current systems are monolithic: one prompted model, or a tight transmitter-receiver pair, must encode meaning, adapt to the channel, and decode at once. Channel damage can then spread through a compressed representation, and faults are hard to locate.

SkillCom defines four skills: semantic abstraction, channel-adaptive transmission, receiver-side repair, and task execution. Typed interfaces between semantic units connect them, so transmission works on structured units, not one text block. Damage stays local to a unit where possible. The modular design aims for systems that are easier to diagnose, swap, and improve piece by piece.
arxiv-2605-02733:
Carlos A. Bonin and three co-authors analyze a relativistic model of contact interactions at two points on a line. The setting is the one-dimensional Dirac equation, with the most general contact interaction placed at two points set symmetrically about the origin. A distributional method fixes the interaction's shape, matching the standard route of self-adjoint extensions, and each point's interaction carries four parameters with clear physical meaning.

The authors focus on interactions that are even or odd under parity, the mirror symmetry of the setup. They investigate when critical and supercritical states appear, along with bound states, confinement, and scattering resonances, for several interactions of special interest. The paper is a careful case study of how much physics a pair of point contacts can hold.
arxiv-2605-02933:
Ye Lu and three co-authors use a language model as the surrogate inside an evolutionary optimizer for costly black-box problems. Each true evaluation is expensive and no gradients exist, so the budget of evaluations is the bottleneck. Surrogate models that predict quality cut evaluations, but classic surrogates need frequent retraining as the population shifts, adding overhead of their own.

Their surrogate judges relations between candidates, cast as a pairwise reading task in context. An anchor-based scheme builds the context in linear, not quadratic, size as the population grows, and votes turn pairwise calls into scores for choosing offspring. A reinforcement pipeline trained on past evolutionary runs fine-tunes the model for this role. On single and multi-goal benchmarks, relation accuracy and final optimization beat strong surrogate baselines and general models.
arxiv-2605-03133:
Wenqin Chen, Kaijie Yang, Ting Cao, Shi-Zeng Lin, Jiabin Yu, and Di Xiao develop a geometric measure for the size of Cooper pairs in superconductors. Pair size is normally set by band spread and the gap, but in flat bands that picture fails and quantum geometry takes over.

They define a pair quadrupole moment whose trace gives pair size, valid for both normal and flat bands. When time-reversal symmetry breaks, Berry curvature adds a key part that metric-only theories miss, and both effects set a lower bound. In rhombohedral graphene, the curvature part can dominate and matches measured coherence lengths.
arxiv-2605-03533:
Panagiotis Gavriilidis and George C. Alexandropoulos present a consistent model for 2D waveguide-fed metasurface antennas. It also works in the near field. Companion work needs an analytic base that respects power balance. Earlier treatments did not fully enforce that balance.

Built on the discrete dipole method, it derives power-consistent constraints on the magnetic polarizability tensor. Closed forms for effective values follow. Full-wave simulations validate the model for multi-feed settings. The near-field extension enables accurate radiating near-field predictions, completing the analytic toolkit for this antenna class. The model gives a firm base for the work that builds on it.
arxiv-2605-03633:
Pavel Hernández Amaro and five co-authors extend multivariate functional principal component analysis to data whose observation windows differ between subjects. The method, MFPCA, reduces several functional variables at once to their main modes of variation. Standard versions assume every curve is recorded over the same fixed domain, which real studies often violate.

Their approach runs univariate variable-domain analysis for each variable separately, stacks the resulting scores, and smooths the empirical covariance of those scores over domain length. That yields multivariate eigenfunctions and scores that respect varying observation periods. Simulations show clear gains over methods that ignore domain structure, and an application to body temperature and related measures illustrates the practical value.
arxiv-2605-03733:
Stef van Buuren asks whether predicting missing values as accurately as possible is actually a good idea. Imputation methods that minimize mean squared error give accurate point estimates, but the imputed values behave like averages and shrink the data's natural variability. That shrinkage biases downstream estimates of variance, prevalence, correlation, slope, and explained variance.

Van Buuren shows that adding noise, in an amount proportional to the mean squared error, can remove these biases. In a multivariate normal toy example and simulations, predictive imputation biased results systematically while stochastic imputation stayed unbiased. Popular tools including missForest, softImpute, and mice showed the same pattern, arguing that error alone is a poor quality measure.
arxiv-2605-03933:
Kishore Ram Sathia and Marco Giovanni Giometto propose new formulae for the height of the turbulent boundary layer in hurricanes, the layer whose processes drive air-sea exchange of momentum, heat, and moisture. Boundary layer height is a key input to engineering and meteorological models of hurricane winds and storm strength. Existing models rest on a constant eddy viscosity shortcut, a strong simplification.

Outside the eyewall, they propose one scaling for the neutral case and another for the stable case, built from friction velocity, absolute fluid vorticity, and the Brunt-Väisälä frequency. The formulae are derived analytically. They are validated against large-eddy simulations and field observations. They predict heights to within a few percent on average. They also collapse velocity profiles well away from the surface.
arxiv-2605-04033:
Melki Bino studies a hybrid approach to Boolean satisfiability solving, the core problem behind hardware verification, cryptanalysis, and test-pattern generation. Modern conflict-driven clause-learning solvers are highly effective, yet satisfiable instances can still demand heavy conflict analysis before productive regions of the search space appear. The hybrid adds a stochastic front end to guide that search.

A probabilistic-bit Ising sampler proposes high-agreement literals, which are passed to the CDCL solver as temporary assumptions, while correctness is preserved through CDCL fallback. On controlled-backbone random 3-SAT benchmarks, the hybrid cut median conflicts and propagations by roughly four fifths relative to pure CDCL. The benefit proved distribution-sensitive, helping only certain instance classes, so the author also reports exploratory machine-learning gates that predict when hybrid solving is likely to help.
arxiv-2605-04233:
Andreas Crivellin and four co-authors review hints that more Higgs-like particles may exist beyond the one found in 2012. They focus on two possible masses, near ninety-five and near one hundred fifty-two gigaelectronvolts, where collider data show more events than expected.

The weaker hint is seen mainly when the particle decays into two photons, and its source is still unclear. The heavier hint often appears alongside charged leptons, jets, and missing energy, which fits a three-part Higgs model. The authors also note a top-quark decay pattern that current data slightly prefer under that model.
arxiv-2605-04633:
A. Feldmeier-Krause and five co-authors map the motions of stars at the centre of the Milky Way and test a modelling method normally used on other galaxies. The centre hosts a dense nuclear star cluster around the supermassive black hole Sgr A star, nested inside a larger nuclear stellar disc, and each dominates the mass at a different scale.

They extract kinematic maps from integrated starlight across the inner region, rather than tracking individual bright stars as most past work did. An orbit-based code then builds libraries of stellar orbits in a trial gravitational field and matches the maps. The exercise checks whether the standard method for distant galaxies recovers the known Galactic centre.
arxiv-2605-04933:
Shuanglong Kan and Sebastian Ertel build a formal meaning for the RISC-V instruction set inside the Rocq proof assistant, aimed at checking compilers and hardware against each other. An instruction set is the contract between the two, and RISC-V is now used from embedded chips to cloud machines. Earlier formal versions served hardware tooling but lacked machine-checked instruction properties.

Their semantics uses interaction trees, which let compiler and hardware behaviour be compared in one framework. It covers a wide range of RISC-V extensions, with correctness lemmas checked by machine. An extracted simulator passes the standard RISC-V test suites, and three case studies show cross-level verification in action.
arxiv-2605-05033:
Dan-Andrei Geba, Alexandrou Himonas, and Curtis Holliman prove that a family of wave equations with cubic nonlinearity breaks down at exactly the borderline smoothness level. The b-Novikov equation belongs to the Camassa-Holm family, and earlier work had settled most cases: solutions behave well above the critical space and badly below it. The critical case itself stayed open.

The authors prove norm inflation in that critical Sobolev space, meaning small starting data can produce solutions that grow without control in the relevant measure. That result completes the well-posedness theory for the equation. Readers interested in sharp thresholds for nonlinear wave equations will find the closing argument of a long case split here.
arxiv-2605-05133:
Xiaoyu Jiang and four co-authors scale multi-output Gaussian processes, a chance-based method for modelling many linked outputs at once, to truly large output spaces. Existing versions stay tractable only by using narrow kernel forms that limit what patterns they can express. Their model instead builds a flexible deep kernel from inputs plus per-output latent values mapped through a controlled neural network.

Paired with stochastic variational inference, the framework keeps cost manageable while keeping real links between outputs. Benchmarks include climate work with more than ten thousand outputs and sparse spatial transcriptomics data. In both settings the method beat baselines on accuracy and speed, the authors report.
arxiv-2605-05333:
Keshav Dasgupta and Radu Tatar explore how a non-supersymmetric string theory could arise from M-theory on a wedge-shaped space. Their construction uses a seven-dimensional manifold with G2 structure, viewed as a deformed K3 fibration over a three-dimensional base. The geometry has a pinched circle structure that shapes the physics.

They show the manifold's torsion classes neatly describe both its twist and the breaking of supersymmetry in four dimensions. Two different reductions lead to Type 0A and heterotic theories on non-Kähler spaces. A duality between them may hold in the supersymmetric limit, but the authors urge caution beyond it.
arxiv-2605-05433:
Kazi Ranjibul Islam and Andrey Chubukov analyze the collective modes of an unusual superconductor. Here pairing is carried by long-range nematic fluctuations, and the energy gap vanishes on four arcs of the Fermi surface. The authors derive how the pair susceptibility behaves at finite momentum and frequency deep in the superconducting state.

They study both the phase and amplitude channels of the response. In each channel the pole structure differs in kind from a conventional s-wave superconductor. That difference produces a highly unconventional dispersion for the collective modes, setting this nematic system apart from standard BCS behavior.
arxiv-2605-06033:
Andrés Castro Torres, Joan Giner-Miguelez, and Mercè Crosas measure how artificial intelligence has spread through global science. They analyze over 227 million scholarly works from OpenAlex, spanning 1960 to 2024 across four domains and 46 fields. A two step classification pipeline separates real use of AI as a method from mere mentions of AI terms.

Adoption grew in an exponential pattern after 2015, but stayed tied to a few topics close to computer science and standard statistics. AI supported work drew an unwarranted citation premium and faced much higher retraction rates than other work. Wealthy countries lead in AI papers per person, while a belt of global South countries leads in adoption relative to national output. The authors urge better practice on openness and ethics.
arxiv-2605-06233:
J. Kimak and sixteen co-authors separate magnetic from optical signals in the ultrafast dynamics of two antiperovskite materials. These non collinear antiferromagnets host chiral spin textures that drive effects like the anomalous Hall effect without net magnetization. Pump probe laser experiments on thin films of Mn3NiN and Mn3GaN show dynamics that depend strongly on probe geometry, mixing several contributions in each measured signal.

Using polarization resolved measurements and full optical modeling, the team split magnetic and non magnetic parts exactly. In Mn3NiN the field dependence traces to domains shifting under their piezomagnetic moments, an effect absent in Mn3GaN. Warming changed the quenching dynamics of Mn3NiN from one step to two steps. The contrast between the two materials clarifies which signals truly report on magnetism.
arxiv-2605-06433:
Selin Ceydeli, Rui Wang, and Kubilay Atasu address money laundering detection when transaction graphs cannot be pooled across banks. Graph neural networks spot laundering patterns well, but they normally need central access. Training locally instead creates gaps between local and central representations, and patterns crossing bank boundaries can become invisible.

Their layer-wise exchange framework has clients swap node representations during forward passes and adjoints during backward passes, without sharing raw features or labels. Under shared parameters they prove the result matches centralized training. Experiments on directed multigraphs with laundering patterns show per-step exchange works best, with per-epoch exchange still practical.
arxiv-2605-06533:
Piotr Kozicki and Alex Kavvos extend classic logic dualities from systems to relations between systems. Kripke semantics for many logics arises from dualities linking relational frames, read as machines or state systems, with algebras of logical statements on them. Relations such as bisimulation, which says two systems behave alike, had no matching predicate-side story.

The authors build relational versions of Tarski duality for classical propositional logic and Thomason duality for modal logic, both in infinitary form. Well-behaved relations between systems then match relations between their statements. They also sketch a proof system that relates formulas across other systems using these dualities.
arxiv-2605-06733:
Jinqian Chen, Chang Liu, and Jihua Zhu fix a subtle flaw in federated LoRA, where many clients fine-tune a shared model with low-rank adapters and send updates to a server. Averaging the adapter factors directly is unreliable. The same update can be split into factors in infinitely many equivalent ways. So the average changes with arbitrary coordinate choices, even when the real update does not.

Their GLoRA method instead estimates a consensus update subspace from client geometry and aggregates updates in shared reference coordinates, staying in low-rank form. It can also serve adapters of different ranks to clients with different capacities. On GLUE and SuperNI benchmarks it beats federated baselines under varied data, resources, and unseen tasks.
arxiv-2605-06933:
Sepideh Avizheh and four co-authors present MAGIQ, a governance system for multi-agent AI that is designed to resist quantum attacks. Agents must follow their owners' rules for communication, and owners need proof of what agents said. At the same time, standard encryption methods face retirement as quantum computing advances.

MAGIQ lets users set rich policies and budgets for agent sessions, including group sessions. It enforces those rules with post-quantum cryptography and keeps agents accountable through message attribution. The authors formally prove the system's correctness and security, then measure its overhead against a leading framework. They call it a first step toward quantum-safe agent governance.
arxiv-2605-07133:
Jingjing Zhou and nine co-authors benchmark graph anomaly detection under realistic deployment strain. Finding odd nodes in networks matters for fraud detection and platform governance, yet most benchmarks use small, tidy graphs. Their testbed adds three stresses: million-node graphs, extremely rare anomalies, and missing node attributes.

Nine representative models were evaluated on variants built from five graphs, including industrial data. Most graph neural methods could not scale to million-node graphs, and detection collapsed when anomalies became realistically rare. Reconstruction models proved sensitive to how missing attributes were filled. The authors release the benchmark as a diagnostic tool for building sturdier systems.
arxiv-2605-07233:
Praneeth Vepakomma and three co-authors learn a regression model from devices that each hold exactly one data sample. Fitness trackers and body sensors fit that pattern. Standard federated learning fails when a local update rests on a single point, and privacy noise weakens it further. Their method changes what devices send.

Each client adds one carefully calibrated noise perturbation to its sample, then shares a transformed version with the server. Aggregated, those representations yield a gradient update that matches the non-private centralized one in expectation. Devices with almost no data can thus help train accurate models without exposing their raw samples.
arxiv-2605-07333:
Zixuan Xie and five co-authors give the first theory of in-context reinforcement learning for standard softmax transformers. Earlier work simplified attention into a linear form that real models do not use. This paper keeps the standard softmax attention and asks what method a transformer pass really runs in that setting.

With certain parameters, each layer performs one update of a new weighted softmax time-difference method, which contains earlier methods as special cases. Scoring error shrinks as layers grow, under a stated shrinking condition. Those settings also minimize a pretraining loss globally, which explains why they emerge in tests with trained models.
arxiv-2605-07533:
Shenbin Qian and Yves Scherrer ask why large language models translate poorly between low-resource languages. Most earlier work measured translation quality or tried to raise it, without pinning down when and why failures happen. The pair instead open up the models and study how they use their vocabularies during translation.

They tested fifteen models, including four reasoning models, across twenty-two language pairs, and found pairs not centered on English score consistently worse. Their new measure, Token Activation Rate, tracks how fully a model uses its language-specific tokens, and low rates line up with poor translation. Reasoning models generated extra tokens for low-rate languages, though the benefit for quality varied by model.
arxiv-2605-07733:
Srinivas Kumar Ramdas and five co-authors present a production machine learning system that matches trucks to full-truckload shipments from GPS data alone. Matching underpins real-time tracking and arrival estimates, but missing or corrupted vehicle identifiers break traditional methods and leave shipments invisible. Their system, ITM 2.0, treats matching as a probabilistic ranking problem.

GPS pings are discretized with Uber's H3 hexagonal indexing to build route similarity features, combined with timing information and ranked by a LightGBM model with threshold post-processing. Against rule-based baselines it improved precision by twenty-six points in North America and fourteen in Europe while doubling coverage. Deployed at Project44, it tolerates geocoding errors up to a kilometer and sparse ping streams.
arxiv-2605-07833:
Simon Grimm and five co-authors release a faster global chemical equilibrium code for planets whose atmospheres exchange material with molten interiors. Super-Earths and sub-Neptunes can keep magma oceans for long periods, and reading their observed atmospheres requires models that couple air chemistry to the interior in step.

A gradient-based optimizer cuts the cost of solving the chemical network by more than a hundredfold, letting large population studies run. Applying the code to synthetic planets, they find atmospheric mass and metal content are set mainly by the temperature at the atmosphere-magma boundary and the water budget. Gathered hydrogen, by contrast, mostly sinks into the interior. For water-bearing planets, the heat-resistant ratios of magnesium, silicon, and iron strongly steer carbon between gas, silicate, and metal.
arxiv-2605-07933:
Viacheslav Meshchaninov and six co-authors train the latent space and the diffusion model together for text generation. Latent diffusion draws interest for language because it denoises whole sequences in parallel, but everything depends on building the right latent space, which is usually fixed in advance by a separate autoencoder.

Their LDLM reshapes a pretrained language model's internal forms with a trainable encoder, and trains encoder, diffusion model, and decoder jointly. Naive joint training fails, producing a poor model. Their recipe adds a mean-squared decoder loss, diffusion-to-encoder warmup, adaptive timestep sampling, and noise at the decoder input, with ablations showing each piece matters. On OpenWebText and LM1B it beat existing discrete and continuous language models while writing several times faster.
arxiv-2605-08233:
Tommaso Dreossi, Christopher Bryant, Hao Liu, Nathan Mirman, and coauthors generate radio-frequency circuit layouts from desired scattering parameters. Inverse design here is high-dimensional and ill-posed. Earlier generative methods handled only single-layer boards. They also used only binary metal patterns.

The new framework designs two-layer copper layouts with vias on a small board. It uses grayscale metallization below pixel size across a wide frequency band. Hard limits on feed spots are enforced with an annealed projection step. Conditioning can mix partial specs, port placements, material traits, and a reference layout. Candidates appear in seconds and match targets closely. Two fabricated designs validate the pipeline in hardware.
arxiv-2605-08333:
Pengzhou Chen and Tao Chen tune retrieval-augmented generation systems as one coupled problem. A RAG pipeline carries many settings. They split between its retriever and its generator. The two sides interact as a pair. Tuning either side alone leaves gains on the table. Testing full setups is slow and costly too. A joint method has to be smart about where it spends its time.

Their CDS4RAG framework gives the problem a cyclic dual-sequential form. Retriever settings and generator settings are tuned in turns. Each cycle inherits seeds from the last. Fine-grained budget rules spend tests where they help most. The framework is algorithm-agnostic. Other general optimizers can plug in. The authors report faster convergence than black-box approaches.
arxiv-2605-08433:
Ian Lewis, Zhen Liu, and Ishmam Mahbub study electroweak restoration. It is the high-energy regime where the broken electroweak theory starts behaving like its unbroken parent. In that limit, producing longitudinal gauge bosons becomes equivalent to producing Goldstone bosons. That simplifies some amplitudes and reshapes others.

The authors work through fermion collisions that produce pairs of longitudinal bosons. They also treat a boson plus a Higgs. The settings are the Standard Model and two extensions. One is the linear SMEFT, and one is the nonlinear HEFT. A general discussion of amplitudes and cross sections shows where the effective theories agree. It also shows where their structures pull apart.
arxiv-2605-08733:
Ke He, Le He, and three co-authors build SoftGAC, a reinforcement learning method whose actor generates expressive actions in a single network pass. Diffusion and flow actors capture complex action patterns but hide their densities and demand costly repeated evaluations with unstable long backpropagation chains. SoftGAC instead uses one stochastic feedforward network with internal Gaussian bridge layers, making the soft objective exact in path space.

An analytic regularizer compares the actor against a high entropy reference process for both improvement and value learning, with no endpoint entropy estimate needed. At parameter budgets matching strong rivals, returns on hard continuous control tasks match or beat diffusion and flow policies at far lower inference cost.
arxiv-2605-08833:
Mengqi Li, Wensheng Lin, Jinshuai Yang, and Lixin Li design FRACTAL, a sequence architecture that remembers the distant past without going deaf to sudden recent changes. State space models built on classic polynomial projections face a forced trade: uniform weighting dilutes fresh signals, while fading weighting forgets global context. Fractional measure theory supplies projection operators with a tunable singularity that sharpens recent sensitivity while keeping scale invariant memory structure intact.

Built inside a simplified diagonal state space design through careful input initialization, the method captures several time scales at once. On the Long Range Arena benchmark it averages about eighty seven percent, beating the S5 model and shining on the hierarchical ListOps task. Long sequence modeling gains memory with both depth and reflexes.
arxiv-2605-09233:
Zeng and seven colleagues make complex image editing robust by breaking tangled tasks into simpler steps, without letting errors compound. Single turn editing tries all edits in one pass, often gets the task wrong and causes stray edits, while step by step editing splits the task but suffers piling errors. The team studies both methods under one in context framework, asking how step by step splits balance against error build up drawbacks.

They build fake data that creates tasks of varied hard levels, making a large set of high quality split runs. Training on fake data shows well designed methods let step splits keep getting better even as task hard levels rise. Split skills from fake tasks transfer to real images when co trained with real world data, showing sim to real gains. The work promises broader complex editing across domains through careful splits, not single pass heroics.
arxiv-2605-09333:
Corradetti studies the interplay of the Coxeter-Dickson E8-order, para-octonions, and real Okubo algebra. He proves the Coxeter-Dickson order stays closed under the para-octonionic product, recovering a genuine integral system over the integers with the E8 lattice underneath.

The Okubo product behaves differently and more arithmetically: it forces square-root-of-3 coefficients and does not preserve the same integer order. After a diagonal 2-adic scaling, a closed order over the square-root-of-3 integers appears, casting a 2-primary conductor sublattice of E8 as its direct metric shadow, not E8 itself. E8 returns only through 2-adic saturation, equivalently gluing, and that recovery is metric-arithmetic rather than multiplicative. The work places integral structures in eight-dimensional division algebras on a precise footing, separating the para-octonionic case from the Okubo case.
arxiv-2605-09633:
Wang and four colleagues studied robot teams that must keep patrolling a set of places without end, giving busier places higher priority. Their goal was to shrink the worst waiting time, weighted by how important each place is, across an endless patrol. The paper works on weighted graphs, maps where places are nodes and travel routes are edges with lengths.

The authors showed that the usual worst-case goal can hide poor early behavior behind strong long-run results. They therefore proposed a family of goals focused on tail performance, the bad stretches. They proved key facts about these goals, including that best patrol plans exist and can be matched closely by repeating plans. They then turned the problem into a standard decision model and built learning methods plus a test platform, M2Bench, for robot patrol teams.
arxiv-2605-09733:
Clerici and eight colleagues mapped the shapes of 246 massive, compact, quiet galaxies in the nearby universe, picked as outliers in mass, velocity, and size relations. Using g-, r-, and i-band images from the Hyper Suprime-Cam survey, they compared these galaxies with average-sized quiet galaxies matched in mass, star formation, distance, and color. Both groups were mostly S0 galaxies, a lens-shaped type between spirals and ellipticals.

Three-part models, bulge plus disk plus envelope, fit 75 percent of the compact galaxies but only 7 percent of the controls. Their disks were far more compact, while bars appeared in 29 percent of controls and none of the compact set. The envelope's wide range of shapes points to either a stellar halo or a thick disk. Compact quiet galaxies, the authors conclude, are small but structurally complex.
arxiv-2605-09833:
Nguyen and four colleagues studied cross-domain lossy compression through minimum entropy coupling, with rate and class constraints. An encoder sees samples from a damaged source domain, while the decoder must produce outputs matching a set target distribution and preserve facts needed for a downstream classification task. Instead of minimizing per-sample error, the objective maximizes coupling strength between source and rebuild.

With shared randomness, the authors set up a rate-constrained coupling problem and showed the middle step can be dropped without loss, yielding an equal fixed coupling. Closed forms followed for Bernoulli sources, with and without class constraints. A neural repair system using quantization, entropy models, distribution match, and classification regularization showed on MNIST super-resolution and SVHN cleaning that higher rate improves class scores and yields richer rebuilds.
arxiv-2605-10033:
Saha and two colleagues showed that single layers of transition metal dichalcogenides make a strong platform for seeing the orbital Nernst effect. The orbital Nernst effect is a side orbital current set off by an applied heat gradient. Like the orbital Hall effect, it needs no spin-orbit coupling. Theory results from a low-energy valley model highlight the key role of Fermi-level states.

Adding spin-orbit coupling gives a spin Nernst effect, which grows with the strength of spin-orbit coupling and dies without it. Full Brillouin-zone tight-binding math for single-layer 2H-MoS2 and 2H-NbS2 backs the theory results. Both effects appear in MoS2 only with electron or hole doping, while they are present by nature in metallic NbS2. Orbital and spin Berry curves sit at the centre of the effects, doping tunes the signals, and the paper sketches a lab setup.
arxiv-2605-10233:
Vincent Knight brings game theory to the television game The Traitors. A small group of Traitors who know each other faces a larger group of Faithful who do not. His 2026 paper asks how the Faithful should vote at banishment. Random votes are optimal in theory, yet they let colluding Traitors hide inside the noise.

Knight proposes Vote-Left. Players vote in turn for the following survivor, cycling through the group. Under full compliance each survivor gets exactly one vote, so any deviation stands out at once. Paired with a simple punishment rule, the protocol forms a Perfect Bayesian Equilibrium whenever the Faithful hold a strong numbers advantage. Across televised setups it roughly triples the Faithful win chance over random voting when Traitors collude.
arxiv-2605-10333:
Ankur Barsode presents a diagnostic tool for choosing between competing hypotheses in physics and astronomy. The usual approach computes the Bayes factor, the ratio of evidences for data under each hypothesis, and reads it as posterior odds or as a ranking statistic for a frequentist test. His 2026 paper describes the BB relationship, linking a Bayes factor to its distributions under both hypotheses, expressed as a plot.

Using gravitational-wave astronomy examples, With wave examples, Barsode shows BB plots checking Bayes-factor math, catching errors that rough methods might hide. The relationship may also estimate background distributions of the Bayes factor cheaply, even analytically in some cases. Applied to wave-optics lensing of gravitational waves, the technique extrapolates the background from the GWTC4 catalog to bound the significance of event GW231123 at roughly 4.1 sigma.
arxiv-2605-10533:
Marie Brockschmidt and seven colleagues measure which factors act as confounders in causal work. Confounders influence both treatment choice and outcomes. Unlike in random clinical trials, the treatment choice mechanism in observed studies is not known, so it is unclear which factors act as confounders. Their 2026 paper introduces ConfoundingSHAP.

ConfoundingSHAP is a Shapley-based method for giving confounding strength to individual factors. It has two parts. First, a Shapley game aimed to infer the confounding strength of factors, differing from standard SHAP explanations on causal targets such as treatment effect spread, which are ill-suited for this task. Second, a scalable TabPFN-based estimation that avoids full refits, needed because the task requires checking the value function over many adjustment sets. Across various datasets, ConfoundingSHAP gives useful accounts of which observed factors drive confounding, helping to identify which patient traits are needed to make treatment groups matched.
arxiv-2605-10633:
Krishak Aneja and four colleagues map how personality structure guards against emergent misalignment in language models. Fine-tuning models on benign narrow data can sometimes trigger broad harmful behaviors. Prior work ties these failures to particular directions in activation space, but not to the model's wider persona. Their 2026 paper maps the latent personality space through profiles like the Big Five, Dark Triad, and model-specific behaviors.

The authors show the semantic geometry holds steady from aligned models to their corrupted fine-tunes. Directions isolating social valence, such as the Evil persona vector and a new Semantic Valence Vector, function as intrinsic guardrails. Ablating them drives misalignment rates above 40 percent, while amplifying them suppresses failures to less than 3 percent. Vectors extracted in advance from an instruct-tuned model transfer zero-shot to regulate misalignment in corrupted fine-tunes.
arxiv-2605-10733: Andrada Pojar and Constantin-Cosmin Todea study a tool for measuring how algebras with symmetry can bend. For one finite group acting on another, they find conditions for the first equivariant cohomology of the group algebra to be non-trivial. This holds when the field size divides the group order. They also show this cohomology equals a relative Ext group, a standard tool in relative homological algebra.
arxiv-2605-10833: Zhao and eight colleagues introduce MMVIAD, the first continuous multi-view video set for industrial anomaly detection. It holds object-centred two-second inspection clips with about 120 degrees of camera motion. It covers 48 object types, 14 settings and 6 anomaly types. It supports four tasks, from detection to defect classification. Current video models still fall far short of human skill here, and the team's two-stage training lifts its VISTA model from 45 point 0 to 57 point 5 on unseen data.
arxiv-2605-10933:
Chenyang Song and five colleagues design DECO, a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture meant to match dense transformers on devices with tight storage and memory. Expert models scale capacity cheaply in compute, but their huge total parameter count chokes end-side deployment.

DECO routes with a flexible ReLU-based scheme plus learnable per-expert scaling that balances routed and shared experts, and adds NormSiLU, an activation that steadies expert usage and raises sparsity. Activating only a fifth of routed experts, it matches dense performance and beats established expert baselines, with a custom kernel running nearly three times faster than dense code on Jetson hardware. Edge teams get expert scale without the storage penalty.
arxiv-2605-11033:
The TaiScience Research Group tests whether TokaMind, a multi-input transformer trained on tokamak plasma sensor data, transfers to distinct but structurally similar domains. TokaMind had beaten convolutional approaches on fusion benchmarks, and the team asks whether its learned patterns generalize beyond plasma.

Across bearing wear, turbofan wear, and two power-grid phasor data sets, four transfer-friendly traits emerge: dense stable sensor coupling, inside-driven critical failures, observed failure cases, and enough labeled events. Power-grid phasor data matches the profile most directly, and on a 500-event grid benchmark the model reaches an F1 score of about 0.84. Cross-domain teams get a profile for predicting where plasma-trained patterns will travel.
arxiv-2605-11133:
Emma Andersdotter, Daniel Persson, and Fredrik Ohlsson introduce steerable neural ordinary differential equations on homogeneous spaces. These models extend manifold neural ODEs by moving feature vectors that transform under the local symmetry group H. Features are read as sections of associated vector bundles over M equals G over H.

Feature motion becomes parallel transport, giving a coupled system: a flow rule on M plus a steering rule acting on features. Steerable NODEs are G-equivariant when both the flow vector field and the transport connection are G-invariant. The framework also absorbs prior NODE models and continuous normalizing flows on Lie groups. Deep learning researchers get the base for learning continuous-time equivariant dynamics of vector-valued features on these spaces.
arxiv-2605-11233:
Ali Soltani and four co-authors compare model selection criteria for symbolic regression across data regimes. The field seeks math expressions trading accuracy for simplicity with low error on new data, and genetic programming code makes Pareto-optimal candidate sets. But reliable auto choice of solutions that hold up on new data remains open.

The Akaike information criterion, corrected AIC, Bayesian information criterion, minimum description length, and Efron's bootstrap estimate for in-sample prediction error are compared on seven synthetic datasets with Gaussian noise. Entries are ranked by each rule and judged on new-data results. Users get a hands-on guide to which choice rules actually pick expressions that hold up.
arxiv-2605-11533: Xiang and six colleagues introduce C2A, a dataset for turning multimodal clinical check-up reports into Action Cards for patients. Routine reports combine labs, body checks, imaging and visual information, but rarely say what to do next. C2A holds 2,000 scrubbed reports, each card naming one issue, its priority, department, follow-up window, explanation and questions for clinicians. Scoring covers coverage, precision, priority consistency, department and timing accuracy, complexity, usefulness, readability and safety. No model leads on every dimension, though experts judged 84 percent of outputs fully sound.
arxiv-2605-11833: Andrei Tetenov, Ivan Yudin, and Dmitrii Drozdov study self-similar dendrites, branching fractal curves whose finite self-similar boundary defines a finite graph called the sprout. The paper shows that this edge-labeled bipartite graph captures the dendrite's combinatorial properties and its topological structure. In other words, the small finite graph encodes how the branching shape is put together and what kind of space it forms.
arxiv-2605-12033: Amir Subba and Yu Shi probe quantum correlations in top-antitop pairs at the LHC within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory. Reconstructing the spin density matrix from lepton angular distributions, they analyze entanglement, geometric quantum discord, and the Bell parameter across four invariant-mass bins. In the Standard Model, entanglement appears only near threshold below about 400 GeV, while discord persists across all phase space. Anomalous chromo-dipole interactions shift observables mainly near threshold, and the CP-even coupling C2V causes the biggest deformation.
arxiv-2605-12233: Sina Mavali and seven colleagues build TAB, a benchmark for terminal agent task alignment. Terminal agents run tasks from a prompt, but must judge found instructions: useful cues must be followed, misleading ones ignored. Existing benchmarks miss this skill, since agents can look capable by following everything or look robust by ignoring everything. TAB offers 89 underspecified tasks, each with a needed cue hidden in an artifact plus a distractor. Tests on ten agents show a gap between completion and alignment, and defenses that block distractors also block needed cues.
arxiv-2605-12433: Jamet and four colleagues fix two leaks in server instruction prefetching. Modern workloads strain the processor front end, yet prefetchers fall short when page-crossing fetches wait on address translation, and when many fetched code lines prove dead on arrival. Their IP-CaT framework tackles both at once with a small translation prefetch buffer beside the second-level TLB and joint cache management. The design aims to cut translation delays and keep only code lines likely to be reused.
arxiv-2605-12633: Campos, Manton and Mohammadi study collisions of localised oscillons in two classes of scalar field theories with metastable false vacua. Small oscillons are built around the false vacuum, and the force between them fades exponentially with distance, modulated by relative phase. Simulations show reflection, crossing and formation of excited lumps, with resonance windows like those in kink-antikink clashes. In the normal theory, energetic lumps can cross a sphaleron barrier and become a kink pair, starting a transition to the true vacuum.
arxiv-2605-12833: Ye studies time steps in the quantized tensor train format. Quantized tensor trains are a multiscale setup cutting the cost of solving PDEs through low-rank fits. Yet their use is limited, because low-rank fits are hard. In long runs, error buildup from gridding and low-rank fits raises rank and drowns results. Using advection problems for plasma and fields, she tests how time stepper, added damping, and problem form affect quantized tensor train math.
arxiv-2605-12933: Higashiyama, Ouchi, Fujita and Utiyama build ATD-Trans, a Japanese-English dataset of travel writing annotated with geographic detail. It lets researchers score translation quality overall and for place names, across regions inside Japan and abroad. Tests on current language models favour Japanese-enhanced models and show domestic place names in travel blogs pose the greatest difficulty. The dataset supports fairer multilingual access to geographic information.
arxiv-2605-13033: López classifies separable surfaces that are critical points of the Dirichlet energy, surfaces of the form z equals a function of x and y. He restricts to surfaces given implicitly by a sum of single-variable functions set to zero. When the constant vanishes, a large family with interesting symmetries appears. When it does not vanish, the surfaces must be either surfaces of revolution or sums of a function of x and a function of y, with explicit parametrisations obtained.
arxiv-2605-13533: Soichiro Fujii and three colleagues present a categorical account of monads and distributive laws in substructural contexts. They model substructural varying contexts with Tronin's verbal categories W, in a uniform way. They define W-operadic monads, set via the rules in W, and W-commutative monads, invariant under those rules. They give a standard way to build a distributive law ST to TS on Set, valid when S is W-operadic and T is W-commutative. That covers many known and new laws.
arxiv-2605-13633: Lambert Theisen and Satyvir Singh study thermal boundary rules for natural convection and entropy build-up in non-Newtonian power-law fluids. Steady two-dimensional maths from the power-law model and Boussinesq rule are solved with the Gridap.jl finite element tool. Shear-thinning fluids boost heat-driven flow, steepen thermal gradients and raise heat transfer, while shear-thick fluids damp convection. Uniform heating gives stronger wider flows, while non-uniform wavy heating narrows forcing and always cuts total entropy build-up.
arxiv-2605-13833: Hoang-Quan Nguyen, Sankalp Pandey and Khoa Luu propose Quantum Long-focus Memory, a hybrid quantum memory tool growing state-space models. Instead of an old latent state updated through adding motion, QLAM holds the hidden state as a quantum state with sizes encoding an overlap of past data. On ordered variants of image sorting tests like sMNIST, sFashion-MNIST and sCIFAR-10, QLAM always improves over looping rivals and focus-based models.
arxiv-2605-13933: Rudravaram and nineteen co-authors build a self-taught model for brain wiring maps that splits scan-site effects from true biology. Diffusion MRI scans shift with site, scanner and scan rules, which muddies wiring-map study. Most shrink methods blend all shifts into one smooth space. Their mixed latent-space design fades its inner codes before decoding, so the model weighs discrete and smooth parts on its own, with no hand-set size tuning.
arxiv-2605-14033: Olivieri and Hernandez build a sheaf-theoretic frame to spot when an AI agent's scientific theory stops carrying over. Fitting equations to data is not enough: an agent must tell whether its framework still carries over to fresh regimes, or whether its language has grown locally-to-globally blocked. Contexts form a local-to-global structure where source, overlap, target and validation charts are fit, trimmed and tested for gluing. Obstruction is scored through fit residuals, overlap clashes, constraint breaks, limit-relation failures and representation cost.
arxiv-2605-14133: Lai and ten co-authors present ClawForge, a generator-backed benchmark for command-line agents working under state conflict. Interactive benchmarks strain between scalable construction and realistic workflow tests: hand-written tasks cost much to extend, while static prompt tests miss failures that surface only over persistent state. Most existing benchmarks also start tasks from clean state, never testing agents on partial, stale or conflicting artifacts. ClawForge compiles scenario templates, grounded slots, initial state, reference paths and validators into reproducible task specs.
arxiv-2605-14233: Park and six co-authors report eight Little Red Dots at low redshift in DESI, a new sample at redshifts 0.2 to 0.45. JWST revealed abundant compact broad-line emitters largely above redshift four, the Little Red Dots, possibly tracing an unprobed black hole evolution channel. At lower redshifts, where ground-based study is feasible, such objects stayed elusive. Unlike earlier searches for compact sources with specific photometric distributions, this search leans on emission line properties, and the eight sources show spectral features akin to high-redshift Little Red Dots.
arxiv-2605-14333: Yue and twelve co-authors propose InsightTok, a visual token framework for text and face fidelity. Text and faces matter, yet challenge autoregressive generators on tokens. They are the bottleneck: downsampling and quantization discard structures needed for readable glyphs. Standard objectives weakly align with legibility. With a 16k codebook and 16x downsampling, InsightTok beats prior ones in text and face remakes. Gains transfer to InsightAR, producing clearer text and more faithful facial details.
arxiv-2605-14633: Cheng, Ou, Zhu, Zhang, Qiu, Han, Zhang, Li and Zheng demonstrate TESLA, a contactless electromagnetic side-channel attack on smartphone touchscreens. A probe placed near a device picks up emanations from touchscreen scanning that encode touch timing and position. The attack is claimed to recover PIN codes, keyboard input, app categories and handwriting trajectories, with PIN recognition near ninety-nine percent on tested phones including iPhone X and Samsung S10 models.
arxiv-2605-14933: Hantao Nie and five others develop a Riemannian Nyström method for operators on manifolds, curved spaces where tangent planes vary point by point. The low-rank method projects onto tangent subspaces, keeping the good traits of the classical Nyström method, such as positive semidefiniteness. A Haar-Grassmann sketching rule, given without coordinates, stays valid when vectors move between tangent spaces. A randomized Newton-type optimizer built on it cuts costs on SPD and Grassmann manifolds at like accuracy.
arxiv-2605-15033: Dmitry Chistikov and three others ask what can be learned about a social network from samples of opinion updates made in sync. When a fixed number of influencers can block change, as under unanimity rules, they give a fast PAC learning method for bounded influencer counts. When opinions follow the majority of influencers, they prove no fast PAC method exists under standard complexity assumptions. A quick heuristic still recovers consistent networks in over 98 percent of random-graph simulations.
arxiv-2605-15233: Rylan Malarchick offers a six-axis rubric gauging control-plane openness in near-term quantum computing, the layer between gate-level circuits and physical electronics. The rubric is defined so same evidence yields same grades. It is validated by blinded re-grading, an edge-case method, and a published protocol. Tied to IBM's February 2025 removal of pulse-level access, it tracks change over time. Applied to thirteen vendors, it shows harms including lost redo access to pre-2025 pulse tests.
arxiv-2605-15433: Tawsik Jawad, Gowtham Atluri, and Vikram Ravindra test whether attention helps EEG-based diagnosis of neurodegenerative disease, where noisy signals and coarse spatial resolution blur group differences. Spectrally selective features, isolating strengths within primary brainwave bands, let traditional machine learning match or beat state-of-the-art deep models on small datasets. Attention, by contrast, fails to distill stable signatures of healthy neural activity in resting and task EEG. Frequency-selective inputs do not rescue it. Results hold across three resting and one task dataset.
arxiv-2605-15633: Junhan Yu, Yurui Chen, Juan Delgado-SanMartin, Dennis Wang, Hong Pan, and Doudou Zhou develop CORE-Cox, a transfer-learning model for survival risk stratification in small clinical cohorts. It learns shared risk patterns across related outcomes in a large source cohort through a low-rank Cox structure, then adapts them to a smaller target cohort with regularized residual correction. Tested in UK Biobank and intensive-care records, it improved discrimination on most outcomes, raising mean concordance from 0.733 to 0.766 in one cohort and from 0.628 to 0.658 in the other.
arxiv-2605-15733: Tianqiu Zhang and three colleagues build a brain-like model for structure learning. Humans turn experience into structured forms to aid guesses and transfer. The HPC-MEC circuit tracks spatial and idea spaces, yet how it pulls structures from high-dimensional motion is poorly known. Their model pairs an inverse model for extraction with a coupling model that splits links from past scenes. Path integration enables guesses and structure reuse across contexts. The work offers a frame for how brain-like world models build abstract knowledge.
arxiv-2605-15833: Ivan Lahtin and Viktor Zamaraev settle whether near-static temporal graphs allow linear-time exploration. They study always-connected k-edge-deficient temporal graphs, each snapshot connected and at most k edges from a fixed base graph. Prior work gave an O(kn log n) schedule and an Omega(n log k) lower bound,  They prove any such graph admits an O(nk log k) schedule, computable in polynomial time. For constant k this gives order-optimal Theta(n) time, so temporal exploration here keeps static traversal's linear character.
arxiv-2605-15933: Snorre H. Christiansen shows how the cohomology of key Bernstein-Gelfand-Gelfand chains for numerical analysis of partial differential equations follows from a long exact chain connecting cohomology groups. He then extends the result to the non-injective/surjective case through systematic use of short exact chains of complexes and their long exact chains of cohomology groups. Finally, he gives an interpretation in terms of spectral sequences.
arxiv-2605-16033: Ferger considers testing the mean of high-dimensional data when the dimension may grow freely relative to the sample size. His test avoids inverting the covariance matrix, so it suits such wide data. He proves long-run results for fixed and growing dimension by placing observations in Hilbert space. A bootstrap version yields valid tests with no extra assumptions about the shape of the data.
arxiv-2605-16333: Cordeiro tests his toolkit on dynamic projection-mapping and spatial augmented reality, growing about 200 seed results into a citation graph of 2,198 nodes and 8,249 edges. SotA Lens is earlier and broader: researchers often survey a wide field before fixing the narrow protocol a systematic review demands. His network-based method and lightweight toolkit join seed search, DOI-level metadata resolution, citation expansion, graph building, community detection, and human labels. It complements, not replaces, PRISMA, systematic mapping, and bibliometric science mapping, leaving auditable records before that protocol is set.
arxiv-2605-16633: Barry defines a new group of lower-triangular matrices whose columns come from power series, generalizing both the Riordan group and the double Riordan group. Its elements are set by three power series, with sequence bisections and vertically stretched Riordan arrays central to the construction. He gives a production-matrix characterization of the group and sketches higher-order versions built from n-tuples of series. The group is named for Renzo Sprugnoli, a pioneer of Riordan methods in combinatorics.
arxiv-2605-16733: Chen and Sanz-Alonso prove sharp dimension-free concentration and expectation bounds for sample cross-covariance matrices. For sub-Gaussian random vectors, a high-probability operator-norm bound follows the effective ranks of the two marginal matrices. In the Gaussian case, a matching lower bound on expectation holds, allowing arbitrary correlation between the two vectors. The results give tight control of how far a sample matrix can stray from its mean, independent of size.
arxiv-2605-17133: Elkhodary and colleagues attack forged video by comparing what a clip shows, how it moves and how deep its scene looks. Their CAM-VFD system lets appearance features question motion and depth features through cross-attention, exposing mismatches that single-signal detectors miss. On two generated-video benchmarks it tops 93 percent accuracy and holds up under compression and noise, the authors report.
arxiv-2605-17433: Deng and colleagues present VISTA, a source-free test-time tuning framework for multi-sequence MRI segmentation under scanner and protocol shifts. An intervention maker probes inter-sequence consistency by exchanging low-frequency spectra and entropy-localized regions across sequences, while a disagreement-aware labeling scheme gates self-training by voxel reliability. Adapting adult MRI models to African low-field and pediatric cohorts, it beats rivals with Dice gains near two and three points.
arxiv-2605-17533: Santjoko and colleagues propose a spread-out 3D leader-follower formation frame for multi-UAV systems that keeps camera visibility by design. A relative motion model in line-of-sight coordinates drives a tracking controller using only local states. A control-barrier-function safety filter then gently adjusts commanded speeds to keep the leader inside the follower's camera frustum when it can. Gazebo sim runs and Crazyflie hardware tests confirm accurate tracking with strong field-of-view enforcement.
arxiv-2605-17633: Hoai-Chau Tran and colleagues propose SparseSAM, a training-free frame accelerating attention and MLP layers while keeping token identity. Token merging cuts token length yet adds overhead and suffers quality drop under high compression, while sparse attention leaves the MLP dense. SparseSAM adds Stripe-Sort Attention, turning dense attention into static sparse patterns, plus a Residual-Consistency MLP routing only informative tokens through the MLP. Across four benchmarks it loses little accuracy at moderate density and slightly more at lower density, with twice faster inference and less memory.
arxiv-2605-17733: Yimeng Min and Carla P. Gomes study Rectified Flow, a method that builds pairs of points joined by paths meant to run straight. In practice those paths bend and tangle where the learned velocity field expands or shrinks locally. The pair propose divergence-suppressing couplings, an offline fix that tones down the divergent part of the field while pairs are built. The fix is paid once per pair, so deployment still runs plain Euler at the same speed. Tests on flat synthetic cases and image generation show steady gains.
arxiv-2605-18233: X. Feng's 2026 paper presents MIGA, a train-free method for generating infinitely long videos with steady consistency. Frame-level autoregressive designs hold memory constant, but the gap between training and inference plus drifting long-term consistency limit their use. MIGA first aligns the stages by shrinking the noise span fed to the model. Dual consistency repair follows: self-reflection fixes early high-noise frames, while long-range guidance steers generation from later low-noise frames. Tests on VBench and NarrLV show state-of-the-art performance.
arxiv-2605-18333: Alberto Marchisio's 2026 paper adapts quantum leaky integrate-and-fire neurons to short-term multivariate weather forecasting. QLIF-CAST encodes neuron excitation as single-qubit superpositions, driven by rotation gates and relaxation decay, in a hybrid recurrent design. Against a matched classical baseline, it cuts mean squared error by 15.4 percent and mean absolute error by 4.4 percent. Against quantum LSTM and quantum network models on air quality and wind benchmarks, it converges in up to 94 percent less training time. Hardware runs on IBM Marrakesh deviate only 1.2 percent from simulation.
arxiv-2605-18533: Mauro Lucci and two co-authors offer, in a 2026 paper, forbidden propagation sets for the capacitated power dominating set problem. These are patterns that cannot co-occur in any feasible solution. The idea yields a new class of integer linear programs mixing infection-based variables with exponentially many constraints, without big-M constraints. Structural traits, valid inequalities, redundancy-breaking rules, and a lazy-separation routine based on cycle detection follow. Tests on benchmarks up to 14,000 vertices show 1.7-fold faster runs than adapted existing methods.
arxiv-2605-18833: Hadi Fadlallah and three colleagues assess big data quality with knowledge graph embeddings. Existing tools struggle to judge quality in context, leaning on strict matching that misses dataset traits. Their method predicts missing links between a dataset context and quality rules and dimensions in a graph of contextual traits and assessment steps. Weighted by edge attributes, the predictions form a tailored assessment plan. A radiation sensor case study shows the plan can be built for a real dataset.
arxiv-2605-18933: Lei Dong explains why pre norm transformers cope well with three level weights. Sign flips yield about two and three quarter times the sideways energy of equal size shifts. ReLU tilts hidden space in one direction, and the norm layer lays that tilt bare. Ternary error keeps sign, slips through ReLU near unchanged, and real sensitivity stems from rare large features.
arxiv-2605-19033: Ehsan Ahmadi and seven colleagues build RLFTSim for multi agent traffic play. Plain open loop train misses live give and take in hard drive scenes. RLFTSim lines sim runs up with real runs and brews goal led control into scenes. Built on a prior sim model, its prize weighs truth and control. It tops Waymo Open Motion realism, needs far fewer tries than hunt tunes, and shows goal led control.
arxiv-2605-19633: Agrawal and team present optimize_anything, an LLM-based system optimizing any text parameter scored by a function. It spans single-task search, multi-task search with transfer and generalization to new inputs. It discovers agent architectures nearly tripling Gemini Flash ARC-AGI accuracy, and scheduling algorithms cutting cloud costs by 40 percent. It generates CUDA kernels where 87 percent match or beat PyTorch, and beats a reported AlphaEvolve packing solution. Ablations show side information beats score-only feedback, and multi-task search beats independent optimization at equal budgets.
arxiv-2605-19833: Xie and colleagues present Mega-ASR, a framework for speech recognition in real world noise built on large scale acoustic simulation. Models often lose sound grounding under severe compound distortions, dropping words or hallucinating. Their Voices-in-the-Wild-2M data covers seven classic sound effects and fifty four compound cases, trained with sound to meaning progressive fine tuning and dual granularity policy optimisation. Tests beat state of the art systems on adverse condition benchmarks, and on compound scenarios word error rates fall by over thirty percent relative to baselines.
arxiv-2605-19933: Nicolas Klodt and Martin Krejca define the IRIR process. In it, two SIR epidemics run on one graph and each vertex keeps immunity only from its most recent infection. They prove a tight epidemic threshold for survival time, switching from at most quasi-linear in graph size to at least super-polynomial. The result holds for perfectly mixed graphs and extends, for the lower bound, to jumbled graphs including typical Erdős–Rényi graphs of sufficient degree.
arxiv-2605-20033: Rohit Sinha and five co-workers verify reasoning steps of multimodal language models without training a critic. Current training-free methods just average scores from varied sources, ignoring what disagreement among those scores reveals. Their approach treats specialised judges as players in a Nash equilibrium game, where agreement signals a valid step and disagreement flags instability. A closed-form equilibrium score then filters and ranks steps by stability, beating baselines across six benchmarks by a few percent and rivalling learned critics.
arxiv-2605-20133: Clémence Chevignard, Yixin Shen and André Schrottenloher present a quantum algorithm for discrete Gaussian sampling on lattices. Using quantum rejection sampling, it runs asymptotically quadratically faster than its classical counterpart. Its output state can be measured for the distribution or used directly in other quantum algorithms. From it they derive two quantum dual attacks improving on previous ones, incomparable in speed versus memory, the second needing only polynomial classical and quantum memory bar preprocessing. The sampler also speeds up solving short integer solution tasks in any norm.
arxiv-2605-20233: Hanchen David Wang and six co-workers test whether video can signal nursing competency. Their three-stage framework extracts timelines from egocentric video with frozen encoders and few-shot learning, derives sequence features and metrics, and relates these to instructor ratings. Across 22 sessions, 3.8 hours and 493 actions, a DINOv2 backbone with HMM Viterbi decoding reaches 57.4 percent MOF in one-shot recognition. Recognition accuracy trends against competency: more skilled students produce varied, harder-to-classify workflows, while plain sequence features show no link. Recognition accuracy may complement timelines as a signal.
arxiv-2605-20633: Apu Chandra Das and five colleagues test causal estimators when propensity score models are wrong. Propensity methods aim to cut bias in studies where treatment is not assigned at random, but a wrong model can skew results badly. They run many simulations that vary how the score model and the result model are set up. They compare three estimators and four ways to estimate scores, from plain logistic models to tree and margin methods.
arxiv-2605-21033: Guangyi Zhang and three colleagues develop efficient Banzhaf-based data valuation for k-nearest neighbours classification. Data valuation measures the share of single data points to model performance, a basic challenge in machine learning. Game-theoretic methods like the Banzhaf value give principled frameworks for fair pricing but suffer exponential computational complexity. The authors address that challenge with fast routines tuned to finding Banzhaf values in k-nearest neighbour classifiers, first proving the problem is sharp-P-hard, then using local structure.
arxiv-2605-21633: Sayed Amir Mousavi Mobarakeh introduces VRXU-net, a deep learning approach for brain stroke lesion detection and segmentation in T1W MRI. Stroke lesions differ in shape, size, and place, and in grayscale T1W scans they can resemble nearby brain structures, blurring boundaries. His method uses a modified VGG model to spot stroke in 2D slices, then a U-shaped model with residual blocks marks the lesion in each slice. The three plane results combine, and a classifier first cuts needless work on non-lesion slices.
arxiv-2605-21733: Tommy Parisi and colleagues describe a set of permutations whose Kazhdan-Lusztig basis elements admit no reversal factorization. A reversal factorization would split such a basis element into factors from parabolic subgroups, with a denominator polynomial, and would yield cancellation-free combinatorial readings of the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials. No characterization of the permutations that admit such factorizations exists yet. Applying a result of Gaetz and Gao, the authors pin down a set that admits none.
arxiv-2605-22133: Kim and co-authors propose TriProRep, an atom-level protein representation method that improves protein structure prediction. Pretrained representations can improve generation as features or targets, and the authors study them beyond conventional function annotation. It jointly models three aligned views: amino-acid identity, backbone geometry, and local full-atom shape. Their RepSP tests cover homodimer co-folding from apo-chain representations, values of homodimer-derived properties, and monomer results. Across these tasks it beats sequence-only and prior models.
arxiv-2605-22233: Birch, Régnier and Morton tackle a bias in solar prominence detection, where detectors leaned on the colour map of one ultraviolet channel instead of real features. Their pipeline rebuilds each image from three views, grey full disk, enhanced corona and disk removed, while correcting instrument wear across the solar cycle. The best composite model beats earlier box methods and transfers to a second instrument.
arxiv-2605-22533: Ihallaine and team seek an internal magnetic field in a rotating gamma Doradus star for the first time, via Kelvin gravito-inertial modes. Internal fields were recently found in red giants via asteroseismology. Gamma Doradus stars may hold fields in their radiative envelopes. The team uses delta K_a, combining Kelvin frequencies sensitive to magnetic fields. After detection, the team models the spectrum with a magnetic component, via Bayesian methods. A magnetic signature is found in KIC 2309579's envelope. If just above the core, the field would reach about 4 kG.
arxiv-2605-22733: Jose presents HarnessAPI, a Python framework that ends the double maintenance of language model tools as both HTTP endpoints and MCP tool registrations. From one typed skill folder with a handler and Pydantic schemas, it derives a streaming HTTP endpoint, an interactive API interface, and a zero configuration MCP tool in a single process. Dual mode negotiation serves streaming and plain JSON clients from the same handler without changes. Across six sample skills, it cuts framework facing boilerplate by 74 percent against a hand maintained FastAPI plus FastMCP dual stack.
arxiv-2605-22833: Shi and six colleagues describe RAG4Outcome, a retrieval-based framework that predicts how chronic bone infection, or osteomyelitis, will progress after surgery. It pulls together PET-CT imaging reports, surgical and diagnostic records, and follow-up notes, then grounds its forecast in a specialist corpus with expert-guided prompts. Early tests on real cases showed promising accuracy and clinical sense for infection care and post-surgery choices.
arxiv-2605-23033: Batra and four coauthors show that task-relevant information in pretrained models is spread non-monotonically across layers, not confined to the final layer. Using only the last layer or shallow mixtures therefore misses structure that naive aggregation cannot recover. Their Layer-wise Optimal Embedding Selection method picks task-discriminative subspaces by a spectral rule under orthogonality and isotropy constraints. A Geometric Regularization Loss further enforces simplicial structure on class manifolds during fine-tuning. Gains grow with model depth.
arxiv-2605-23433: Zi-Yue Zheng and colleagues compare the basic pulsing of plain neutron stars with hybrid stars that mix nuclear and quark matter. They use two nuclear matter models and a quark model based on Dyson-Schwinger theory, joining the phases with a Gibbs construction. Their headline finding is a clear split in pulse frequency between the two star kinds as rotation slows.
arxiv-2605-23633: Keskin, Yoshida, and van Glabbeek give the first machine-checked liveness proof for synchronous multiparty session types in Rocq. In multiparty session types, a global type describes a protocol. It projects to local types per member, against which processes type-check. The authors represent global and local types as coinductive trees with the paco library, using coinductive subtyping and plain-merge maps. They prove operational correspondence between local contexts and global types, then safety and liveness for linked contexts and sessions. This enables checks of protocol liveness properties.
arxiv-2605-23933: Gao and seven colleagues build a question generator that tailors practice to each student's current knowledge. Their system, KT4EQG, uses knowledge tracing to pick the concept with the most learning payoff. Knowledge tracing models what a student knows from past performance. A language-model generator is then trained to write a question rooted in that concept. Tests on XES3G5M and MOOCRadar show it beats methods with little or no tailoring, producing questions that help students more.
arxiv-2605-24233: Ma models a search user facing a list ordered by a noisy proxy. The user decides whether to pay to inspect another item or stop. Each inspection yields a candidate and refines belief about page quality. The optimal policy is a standout rule: stop once the best find beats expectations. Dynamics collapse to a Markov chain, giving the inspection-depth distribution. Three hidden mechanisms explain stopping: trust, commit, and cut-losses. The same Bayesian view turns inspection depth into a ranking likelihood, and on Baidu logs it beats alternatives.
arxiv-2605-24333: Le, Chernyavsky, and Prinari apply Hirota's two-line method to the discrete Manakov system in its focus regime to build soliton and breather forms. After getting the system's broad two-line form, they obtain basic solitons and basic and mixed breathers. They then construct forms with two solitons, two breathers, and mixed soliton-breather pairs, and discuss all two-body meeting traits. The focus falls on exact rules, pictures, and late-time ways, proving the rich meeting traits of these tidy structures.
arxiv-2605-24733: Yuelyu Ji and others build StepGap, a hybrid decision tree spotting evidence gaps at each step in multi-hop QA. It labels each step contradicted claim, irrelevant evidence, or missing bridge, each tied to a repair action.
